PRO is intraday - every new unrealized high tightens the floor in real time. PRO+ goes back to end-of-day but with no $0 lock. This intraday step-up on PRO is the trickiest TPT rule to manage; PMT's auto-flatten alerts help.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_8_question: Does TPT use static or trailing drawdown on PRO?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_8_answer: PRO uses the same size-specific trailing drawdown ($1.5K-$4.5K) as the Test phase, but it locks against intraday peaks instead of end-of-day. There is no $5K "initial drawdown floor" - the $5K figure in TPT marketing refers to the profit threshold required on PRO to unlock the PRO+ live brokerage upgrade, not a static buffer. PRO+ switches to an EOD-locked drawdown.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_9_question: What is the $5,000 figure on PRO actually about?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_9_answer: $5,000 is the profit threshold on PRO that unlocks eligibility for the PRO+ upgrade - TPT’s LIVE Tradovate brokerage tier with a 90/10 split and EOD drawdown. It is NOT a static drawdown floor. Once you accumulate $5K of profits on PRO (split paid out 80/20 along the way), you can request promotion to PRO+ and trade real money against real exchange execution.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_10_questio: If my account hits the trailing drawdown, can I retry?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_10_answer: Yes. If the Test phase breaches drawdown, the account fails but you can immediately purchase a reset ($100 flat) or use the free reset included with your monthly renewal. PRO accounts can also be reset up to 3 times, with size-scaled reset fees ranging from roughly $449 to $1,499. PRO+ breaches are typically terminal - you’d repurchase a Test from scratch.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_11_questio: Are unrealized P&L counted in the drawdown?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_11_answer: Yes - especially on PRO. PRO’s intraday trailing drawdown locks on unrealized peaks: if your position runs into significant unrealized profit and then gives it back, the floor has already moved up. On the Test phase the drawdown only locks at end of day, so intraday give-backs don’t tighten the floor. Manage stop placement to protect against intraday MAE swings, particularly on PRO.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_12_questio: Does TPT have a daily loss limit?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_12_answer: No. TPT does not enforce a daily loss limit on either the Challenge or PRO. Only the trailing drawdown matters. This is one of TPT's most-cited advantages over Topstep, which enforces a Max Loss Limit per day. You can theoretically lose up to your full trailing drawdown in a single session and still be active until close. If you want to enforce your own daily or weekly profit/loss limits, set these directly in Tradovate — Tradovate allows you to configure daily profit targets and daily loss limits that automatically block new trades once reached. PMT's own daily/weekly limit settings work only on personal/demo Tradovate accounts, not prop firm accounts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_13_questio: Can I lose money during the Challenge and still pass?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_13_answer: Yes - losing days are fine as long as you never breach the trailing drawdown and end-of-day flat is respected. The only outcome that matters is hitting the profit target with the floor intact. Many passes happen after several losing days followed by one strong winning week.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_14_questio: What happens if I cross the drawdown by $1?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_14_answer: Account fails immediately. There's no grace period or rounding. Even a single tick beyond the trailing floor terminates the Challenge or PRO. This is automated - TPT's risk system flat-closes positions at the breach and locks the account. Common trader forums complaint: traders who got within $5-$10 of breach and survived treated it as a win, but most who graze it lose.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_15_questio: Can PickMyTrade enforce my own internal drawdown limits?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_drawdown_15_answer: PMT can help you manage drawdown by ensuring every trade has a stop-loss and take-profit defined via your TradingView alert configuration — this prevents any single position from running unchecked against your drawdown floor. For specific risk management features available in PMT, check the current documentation at docs.pickmytrade.trade.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_dailyloss_title: What Are Take Profit Trader's Daily Loss and End-of-Day Rules?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_1_questio: Why does TPT have no daily loss limit?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_1_answer: TPT's risk model relies entirely on the trailing drawdown plus end-of-day flat requirement. The firm believes traders should self-manage daily risk; the trailing drawdown serves as the ultimate hard limit. This contrasts with Topstep's $1,000-$3,000 Max Loss Limit per day. The trade-off: no DLL is friendlier for swing-style intraday traders but riskier for tilt-prone scalpers.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_2_questio: Do I have to flat all positions at the end of the day?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_2_answer: Yes - the Challenge and most PRO variants require end-of-day flat. Positions must be closed before the daily futures session ends (typically 5:00 PM ET for ES/NQ via the CME maintenance window). Holding past the cutoff auto-fails the account or, on PRO, voids that day's progress.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_3_questio: What time is the TPT end-of-day cutoff?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_3_answer: 4:59 PM ET (Monday-Friday) is the universal flat-by deadline. This corresponds to the daily CME settlement window for equity index futures. For other contracts (energy, metals, ag), the cutoff aligns with their session close. Holding into the maintenance window violates EOD flat.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_4_questio: Are overnight positions allowed at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_4_answer: No - not on Challenge, and not on standard PRO. TPT does offer a Swing PRO variant on some sizes that permits overnight holds with adjusted parameters, but the default Challenge and standard PRO require flat by 4:59 PM ET each day. Most traders trade intraday only.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_5_questio: Can I hold positions over weekends?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_5_answer: No, except on Swing PRO if available. Standard accounts must be flat each Friday by 4:59 PM ET and remain flat through the weekend. Sunday open at 6:00 PM ET is when new positions can be entered for the next week.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_6_questio: Do I have to trade every day?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_6_answer: Not every day, but the Test phase requires a minimum of 5 trading days before you can request the PRO upgrade - even if you hit the profit target on day one. PRO and PRO+ have a minimum activity expectation (typically one trade every 30 days to keep the account active) but no daily mandate.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_7_questio: What happens if I forget to flat a position by EOD?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_7_answer: TPT's risk system auto-liquidates open positions at the maintenance window. On the Challenge, this typically violates EOD flat and fails the account. PickMyTrade includes a Trading Time feature available across all supported broker connections. You can configure specific active trading windows with start and end times (24-hour ET format) — any alerts outside those hours are automatically rejected — no new trades are placed. You can set your trading window to end before TPT's EOD cutoff, preventing any new trades from being placed after that time. Full guide: https://docs.pickmytrade.io/docs/trading-time-settings/
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_8_questio: Does the EOD flat rule apply during the Challenge phase?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_dailyloss_8_answer: Yes. EOD flat is enforced from day one of the Challenge through the entire PRO lifecycle. The drawdown only updates against end-of-day balance, so positions held past the cutoff break the lookup logic and auto-fail. There's no warning - the system simply terminates.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_pass_title: What Are the Conditions to Pass a Take Profit Trader Evaluation?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_1_question: What does it take to pass the TPT Test phase?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_1_answer: Four conditions: (1) hit the size-specific 6% profit target, (2) never breach the trailing drawdown, (3) flat all positions by 4:59 PM ET each day, (4) trade for a minimum of 5 trading days, and (5) respect the 50% best-day consistency rule (your single best day cannot exceed 50% of cumulative profit at request time). Once met, you request the PRO upgrade and pay the flat $130 activation fee.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_2_question: Is there a minimum number of trading days?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_2_answer: Yes - the Test phase requires a 5-trading-day minimum before you can request the PRO upgrade. Even if you smash the profit target in a single session, you still have to log activity across at least five separate trading days. This is one of TPT’s stricter rules versus props like Apex that allow same-day passes.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_3_question: Is there a consistency rule on the Test phase?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_3_answer: Yes - the 50% best-day rule applies during the Test phase. At the moment you request the PRO upgrade, your single best trading day cannot exceed 50% of cumulative profit. So if your best day was $2,000, your total profit at upgrade must be at least $4,000. Spread gains across multiple sessions to stay safe; the rule is checked at upgrade request, not after the fact.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_4_question: Is there a consistency rule on PRO accounts?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_4_answer: No formal consistency rule on PRO at payout - the 50% best-day check applies during the Test phase, not at the PRO payout window. PRO payouts gate on staying above the size-specific buffer threshold (your cushion above the trailing floor) rather than a daily-distribution check. PRO+ payouts likewise focus on profit cushion, not consistency ratios.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_5_question: How quickly can I realistically pass TPT 50?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_5_answer: Realistic median: 8-15 trading days. Aggressive scalpers: 2-5 days. Patient swing-style: 20-30 days. Risking ~$300-$400 per setup with a 1.5R average target produces $3,000 in roughly 8-12 winning trades, achievable in two weeks for most consistent traders.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_6_question: What's the TPT Test phase pass rate?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_6_answer: TPT does not publish official pass-rate statistics. Trader forum anecdotal data and prop-firm review aggregators put it in the 15-25% range, similar to Topstep and Apex. The 1-step format is friendlier than 2-step props, but the 50% consistency rule plus the trailing drawdown locking at $0 catches plenty of traders who run hot in one session then give back gains.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_7_question: Do I need to verify identity to pass?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_7_answer: KYC is required at PRO Account activation, not before. Once you hit the profit target you submit a government ID, sign the funded trader agreement, and complete W-8/W-9 tax forms. Until then you can trade anonymously under your TPT account login. KYC turnaround is typically 24-72 hours.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_8_question: Can I pass on micros only?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pass_8_answer: Yes - TPT permits 100% micro-contract trading throughout the Challenge and PRO. Many TPT 25 and TPT 50 traders pass with micros only because the per-tick risk is 1/10th the mini, fitting tighter trailing drawdowns. There is no rule forcing you to use minis at any size.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_pro_title: How Do Take Profit Trader's PRO and PRO+ Funded Phases Work?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_1_question: What is the TPT PRO Account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_1_answer: PRO is the sim-funded second tier that begins after passing the Test phase. The Test subscription stops, you pay the flat $130 one-time activation fee, and the simulated funded account opens at the size you passed (TPT 25-150). Profits pay out at a flat 80/20 split. The drawdown is the size-specific trailing amount but locks intraday (on unrealized peaks). After $5K of profit on PRO you can upgrade to PRO+.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_2_question: What is the TPT PRO+ Account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_2_answer: PRO+ is the third tier and the only LIVE brokerage account at TPT - a real Tradovate brokerage account with real CME execution, not simulated. You unlock PRO+ after accumulating $5,000 in profits on PRO. The split jumps to a flat 90/10, the drawdown switches to end-of-day (no intraday peak lock), and there is no $0 buffer. PRO+ is unique among major US futures props.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_3_question: How do I activate my TPT PRO Account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_3_answer: Once the Test profit target is met and the 5-day minimum is satisfied, the dashboard shows a "Request PRO Upgrade" button. Click it, complete KYC (passport or DL), sign the funded trader agreement, submit W-8 (international) or W-9 (US) tax form, pay the flat $130 activation fee. PRO credentials are issued within 1-3 business days.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_4_question: What is the profit split on the PRO and PRO+ Accounts?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_4_answer: PRO pays a flat 80/20 across the entire PRO lifecycle - no tiered structure, every dollar earns at 80%. PRO+ pays a flat 90/10. To reach PRO+ you must first earn $5,000 of net profit on PRO (paid out along the way at 80/20); once promoted, all future profits earn at the higher 90/10 rate on real Tradovate live execution. Many traders push to $5K quickly to unlock PRO+.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_5_question: What is the drawdown rule on PRO?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_5_answer: PRO uses the same size-specific trailing drawdown as the Test phase ($1.5K on TPT 25 up to $4.5K on TPT 150), but it locks intraday - every new unrealized high tightens the floor in real time. There is no $5,000 static "initial drawdown" floor; that’s a common misconception. The $5K figure refers to the profit threshold required to upgrade to PRO+.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_6_question: Is the PRO drawdown trailing or static?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_6_answer: Trailing - and stricter than the Test phase. PRO locks the drawdown intraday against unrealized peaks, so a position that runs into profit and gives it back can still tighten the floor before you close the trade. PRO+ switches to an EOD-locked trailing drawdown with no $0 buffer, so the floor only updates at the daily close.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_7_question: When can I request my first PRO payout?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_7_answer: As soon as your PRO account is above its size-specific buffer threshold - the cushion required above the trailing floor for a withdrawal to be approved. There is no fixed "5 winning days" payout gate on PRO (that 5-day rule applies to the Test phase as the minimum trading days). Payouts on PRO are on-demand once buffer is met. Small payouts of $250 or less carry a $50 fee.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_8_question: How many PRO Accounts can I run simultaneously?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_8_answer: TPT permits multiple funded PRO accounts per identity, but consistency tracking flags identical fills across them. As of 2025, the firm tightened copy-trading rules and now caps simultaneous PRO accounts at typically 3-5 per real-name identity. Coordinated identical entries across accounts can trigger a violation review. PRO+ live accounts have stricter caps.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_9_question: Does TPT scale my PRO account up over time?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_9_answer: The "scaling" path at TPT is Test → PRO → PRO+, not an account-size increase. Once on PRO, your notional size remains fixed at TPT 25/50/75/100/150. Upgrading to PRO+ unlocks the 90/10 split and live execution but keeps the same notional. To trade larger, pass another Test phase at a bigger size - TPT does not auto-scale balances like FundedNext.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_10_question: What's the typical PRO account lifespan?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_10_answer: Variable. Best-managed PRO accounts run for months pulling on-demand payouts and eventually graduate to PRO+. Median active lifespan is around 3-6 months on PRO - most traders eventually breach the intraday trailing drawdown after a tilt streak or extended losing period. Trader-forum reports document accounts that ran 12+ months and migrated to PRO+ under disciplined risk management.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_11_question: Can I trade automation on the PRO Account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_11_answer: Yes - personal automation (your own scripts, your own TradingView strategies) is allowed on PRO and PRO+. PickMyTrade routes signals from TradingView to your Tradovate-connected PRO/PRO+ account at $50/month per broker connection. The restriction is on copy-trading and mass-distributed bots - not on your own self-developed automation.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_12_question: What if I breach drawdown on the PRO Account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_12_answer: PRO can be reset - up to 3 times per account, with size-scaled reset fees ranging from roughly $449 (smaller sizes) to $1,499 (larger sizes). After exhausting your 3 resets, the account ends and you’d need to repurchase a Test phase. PRO+ breaches are typically terminal. Always request payouts as soon as you’re eligible to extract earned cash from a still-vulnerable account.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_13_question: Can I trade smaller than my contract limit on PRO?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_13_answer: Yes - the contract cap is a maximum, not a minimum. Trading 1 mini on TPT 50 (cap of 6) is fully allowed and often advisable when starting PRO to dial in process before risking maximum size against the intraday trailing drawdown. PMT users frequently set lower per-account caps in software to enforce conservative early-PRO sizing.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_14_question: Does PRO Account have any monthly fee?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_pro_14_answer: No. Once you pay the flat $130 PRO activation fee, there is no recurring monthly subscription on PRO or PRO+ accounts. The Test subscription stops at conversion. PRO remains active as long as you trade at least one position every 30 days. This zero-monthly-fee structure on funded is a TPT advantage over some competitors.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_payouts_title: How Do Take Profit Trader Payouts Work?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_1_question: How often does TPT pay out?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_1_answer: On-demand. There is no fixed weekly or monthly payout cycle - you can request a withdrawal at any time once you’re above the size-specific buffer threshold. Approved requests typically process within 1-3 business days. This is faster and more flexible than Apex (8-day windows) and Topstep (monthly). On-demand payouts are one of TPT’s biggest differentiators.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_2_question: What is the minimum payout amount?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_2_answer: There is no fixed $1,000 minimum on PRO - payouts are processed once you’re above the size-specific buffer threshold (the cushion above the trailing floor required for withdrawal). Small payouts of $250 or less carry a $50 processing fee, so most traders request in larger batches. PRO+ payouts follow the same on-demand model from the live brokerage account.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_3_question: Is there a maximum payout per cycle?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_3_answer: First payouts are capped - typically the first few on-demand payouts on PRO are limited (commonly to $1,500-$2,500 each) until you build a track record. After completing the initial payout sequence, on-demand requests uncap and you can withdraw the full available cushion. TPT publishes the exact first-payout limits in the funded trader agreement.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_4_question: What payout methods does TPT support?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_4_answer: PayPal, Wise, and Plaid/bank wire are the three core payout rails. PayPal is fully supported (a common point of confusion - TPT lists it on the official payout-method page). Wise handles most international transfers, and Plaid links US bank accounts for ACH-style deposits. Choose your method at payout request time; currency conversion is handled by the rail.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_5_question: How long does a TPT payout take to arrive?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_5_answer: Request submitted → approved within 1-2 business days → funds typically in your account within 1-3 business days for PayPal/Plaid, 3-5 business days for Wise international wires. First payout often takes longer due to KYC review. Subsequent payouts are usually under a week end-to-end. There’s no fixed weekly cycle - request whenever buffer is met.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_6_answer: Yes. TPT issues 1099-NEC for US traders (income reported as self-employment). International traders receive payment statements through PayPal/Wise/Plaid - characterized as performance-licensing fees on PRO and live brokerage income on PRO+. Most jurisdictions treat this as business income (US Schedule C, India ITR-3, UK self-employment). Consult a tax professional locally.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_7_question: Can I leave profits in the account to compound?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_7_answer: Yes. There's no requirement to withdraw on a schedule - payouts are on-demand. Many TPT traders leave profits accumulated to use as a wider trailing buffer. The downside: any breach on PRO forfeits unrequested profits. Most experienced PRO traders extract regularly to lock in earned cash, then re-deploy buffer for the PRO+ upgrade.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_8_question: What's the consistency check at payout?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_8_answer: There’s no formal consistency ratio at the PRO payout stage. The 50% best-day consistency rule applies during the Test phase, checked when you request the PRO upgrade. On PRO and PRO+, payouts gate on staying above the size-specific buffer threshold rather than a daily-distribution check. Many traders confuse the Test-phase rule with a PRO-payout rule.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_9_question: Does TPT have a maximum lifetime payout limit?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_9_answer: No lifetime cap on cumulative profits. Forum threads document several traders pulling $50K-$100K+ from a single PRO or PRO+ account over 12+ months. The 80/20 split on PRO and 90/10 on PRO+ apply indefinitely. The risk is always drawdown breach, not a structural withdrawal cap.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_10_question: Can I see other traders' payout proofs?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_10_answer: Yes. TPT regularly posts payout statements (anonymized totals) on its X account, Discord, and YouTube. Independent payout-proof threads on prop firm forums and futures trader forums also document on-demand receipts. Cross-reference firm-published numbers with community user reports for a fuller picture.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_11_question: What happens to unrequested profits if my account closes?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_11_answer: Forfeited. If your PRO or PRO+ breaches drawdown before you request a payout, all unwithdrawn profits are lost. This is the standard structure across every futures prop. Mitigate by requesting payouts on-demand the moment you’re above buffer, especially in volatile market regimes.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_12_question: How does PMT help with payout planning?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_payouts_12_answer: PickMyTrade users automate consistent setups that produce predictable P&L distributions, helping satisfy the Test-phase consistency rule and accelerate the path to PRO and the PRO+ $5K upgrade threshold. Multi-firm broadcasting (TPT + Apex + MFFU + Topstep simultaneously) lets you collect on-demand payouts from several firms on the same TradingView strategy at $50/month per broker connection for PMT.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_contracts_title: What Are Take Profit Trader's Contract and Position-Sizing Limits?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_1_questio: What are the contract limits per TPT size?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_1_answer: TPT 25 = 3 minis or 30 micros. TPT 50 = 6 minis or 60 micros. TPT 75 = 9 minis or 90 micros. TPT 100 = 12 minis or 120 micros. TPT 150 = 15 minis or 150 micros. Combined positions count toward the limit (e.g., 2 minis + 20 micros = 4 mini-equivalents).
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_2_questio: Can I trade only micro contracts at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_2_answer: Yes. Micros are fully allowed on Challenge and PRO from day one. Many TPT 25 and TPT 50 traders pass exclusively on micros (MES, MNQ, MGC, MCL) because micro tick value ($1.25 for MES) gives finer granularity for tight trailing drawdowns. No rule forces minis at any size.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_3_questio: Is there a "first $10K micros only" rule?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_3_answer: No - verify against current TPT terms. As of 2026 there is no published rule restricting trading to micros until you reach $10,000 cumulative profit. Some users confuse this with Apex’s prior policies. TPT’s split is a flat 80/20 on PRO and a flat 90/10 on PRO+; the actual numerical threshold to remember is $5,000 of PRO profit, which unlocks the PRO+ upgrade.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_4_questio: What contracts can I trade at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_4_answer: All CME products: equity index (ES/NQ/YM/RTY plus micros), energy (CL/NG plus micros), metals (GC/SI plus micros), agricultural (ZS/ZC/ZW), interest rates (ZN/ZB), and currencies. CME crypto futures (BTC, ETH) are typically allowed. Always check the TPT product list for any temporarily restricted contracts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_5_questio: Can I trade options on futures at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_5_answer: No. TPT does not support futures options. Only outright futures contracts and micros are tradable. This is consistent across all major futures prop firms (Apex, Topstep, MFFU). For options strategies, you'd need a regulated brokerage account, not a prop sim.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_6_answer: No - futures only. TPT is a CME-products prop firm; equities, crypto spot, forex spot, and ETFs are not in scope. If you need multi-asset coverage, look at E8 Markets (forex/crypto/futures) or a regulated brokerage. PMT routes equally well to TPT and to forex props if you run both.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_7_questio: Can I scale into positions across multiple legs?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_7_answer: Yes - pyramiding is allowed. You can stack multiple entries up to the size-specific contract cap. Common strategy: enter 2 minis at level 1, 2 minis at level 2 confirmation, 2 minis at level 3 - total 6 on TPT 50. Manage stops carefully because the trailing drawdown sees aggregate position MAE.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_8_questio: Is hedging allowed (long ES + short NQ)?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_8_answer: Cross-product hedging is allowed (ES vs NQ, ES vs YM, etc.) but each leg counts toward your contract limit independently. Same-product opposing positions (long ES + short ES simultaneously) typically net to zero in the position blotter - TPT generally treats this as flat rather than a hedged pair.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_9_questio: Does TPT enforce minimum stop loss on every trade?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_9_answer: No - TPT does not require stops. Many traders wisely use them anyway because the trailing drawdown is unforgiving. If you configure a stop-loss in PickMyTrade's alert setup, PMT will include it on every webhook that fires — this is an optional configuration, not something PMT auto-generates. PMT also works with entry-only alerts. Including a stop in your PMT configuration is strongly recommended.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_10_questi: How does PMT handle TPT contract limits?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_contracts_10_answer: You can configure a fixed contract quantity per account in PickMyTrade's alert setup, which ensures every alert fires with that quantity regardless of what the TradingView signal specifies. Set TPT 50 to 6 minis in PMT's configuration and all webhooks will use 6 minis. If you need dynamic sizing, express it in your TradingView alert payload. Configure once, applied per webhook.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_rules_title: What Are Take Profit Trader's News, Holding, and Reset Rules?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_1_question: Can I trade news events at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_1_answer: Yes - news trading is allowed on both Challenge and PRO. There is no restricted-news list at TPT (unlike FundedNext or FTMO). FOMC, NFP, CPI, GDP - you can hold positions through them. Be aware: spread widening and slippage during major news can blow through stops and breach drawdown faster than during normal sessions.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_2_question: Are there any prohibited trading windows?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_2_answer: No prohibited intraday windows. The only time-based rule is the 4:59 PM ET end-of-day flat. You can trade overnight ETH session, day session, or any sub-window. Many traders avoid the 4:00-5:00 PM low-liquidity hour anyway because spreads widen.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_3_answer: Yes. Scalping (quick in-and-out trades, typically under 1 minute) is allowed. TPT does not enforce minimum-hold-time rules unlike some forex props. Watch the trailing drawdown on PRO - heavy scalp days can trigger the consistency check at payout if a single big-win scalp day inflates your best-day percentage.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_4_answer: Always check Take Profit Trader's official website for the latest compliance guidelines. Many PickMyTrade customers successfully automate their TPT accounts — a small amount of risk is always involved with automated trading on any prop firm.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_5_answer: No. Martingale (doubling-down on losers to recover) and reverse martingale (doubling-up on winners) are explicitly banned in the TPT funded trader agreement. TPT's risk team reviews accounts that show progressive position-sizing patterns aligned with martingale signatures and can void payouts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_6_answer: No. Grid trading - placing layered limit orders above and below the current price expecting reversion - is prohibited. The TPT risk team flags grids because they often combine with martingale-style averaging. Traditional discretionary or single-entry algorithmic strategies are fine; layered grid orders are not.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_7_question: Can I trade weekends or holidays?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_7_answer: Sunday open at 6:00 PM ET begins the new trading week. Saturday is closed (CME does not run weekend sessions for futures except crypto). Federal holidays follow CME schedule - typically reduced hours or full close. TPT auto-flatten and EOD rules adjust to the holiday session calendar.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_8_answer: No special rule, but slippage during overnight ETH or holiday-thin sessions can cost more than normal. TPT's sim quotes mirror the live order book; a 5-tick slip during the Globex graveyard hours is common. Most disciplined traders restrict their PRO trading to the 9:30 AM-4:00 PM ET RTH session for tightest spreads.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_9_question: Are reset rules different on Test vs PRO vs PRO+?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_9_answer: Yes - different on each tier. Test breaches reset at $100 flat (or use the one free reset included with each monthly renewal). PRO breaches can be reset up to 3 times at fees ranging from roughly $449 to $1,499 by size. PRO+ breaches are typically terminal - repeat from a new Test phase. This is why traders prioritize on-demand payouts on PRO and treat the PRO+ live account as a finite resource.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_10_question: Does TPT have a same-side rule like Apex?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_rules_10_answer: No same-side rule. Apex's rule restricts identical entries across multiple Apex accounts. TPT's tightening on copy-trading is similar in spirit but enforced through a different consistency-tracking mechanism at payout review, not as a hard intraday block. PMT manages this with smart per-account routing rules.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_automation_title: Does Take Profit Trader Allow Automation, Bots, and Copy Trading?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_1_questi: Is automated trading allowed at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_1_answer: Yes. Personal automation - your own TradingView strategies, your own NinjaTrader indicators, your own Python or scripts - is fully allowed on both Challenge and PRO. PickMyTrade is the dominant TradingView-to-Tradovate automation bridge for TPT users at $50/month per broker connection across all your TPT accounts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_2_questi: Are commercial bots and EAs permitted?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_2_answer: No. Mass-distributed commercial bots, paid-signal-service EAs, and group-shared algorithms are prohibited. The reasoning: TPT can't fund the same strategy across hundreds of accounts because the firm bears net risk on the cumulative book. Personal proprietary scripts you wrote yourself are fine.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_3_answer: Two specific patterns: (1) identical fills across multiple TPT accounts (your own or others'), (2) following a signal-service master account where multiple strangers receive the same trades. TPT tightened both throughout 2024-2025. The risk system flags suspiciously aligned timestamps and identical order parameters across accounts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_4_questi: Did TPT recently tighten copy-trade rules?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_4_answer: Yes. Through 2024-2025, TPT publicly tightened multi-account copy-trade enforcement. New language in the funded trader agreement explicitly bars cross-account replication. Cap on simultaneous funded accounts per identity dropped from "unlimited" to a 3-5 functional cap. This was an industry-wide trend (Apex did the same).
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_5_questi: Can I run the same TradingView strategy on TPT and Apex?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_5_answer: Yes - across different firms is generally permitted. The copy-trade restriction applies within TPT (multiple TPT accounts), not across firms. PMT lets one TradingView alert broadcast to TPT, Apex, MFFU, Topstep, and Bulenox simultaneously - a common multi-firm strategy. Each firm sees only its own account's fills.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_6_questi: Does PMT trigger TPT's copy-trade detection?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_6_answer: If you run a single PMT account routing to one TPT PRO, no - that's standard automation, identical to placing trades manually. The risk emerges only when you mirror identical fills across multiple TPT PROs. PMT supports per-account jitter (random 200-500ms timing offsets, slight contract variations) to differentiate fills if you must run multiple TPT accounts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_7_questi: Are signal services allowed on TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_7_answer: Subscribing to signal services and acting on them manually is permitted. Direct mass-broadcast where the same signal hits dozens of TPT accounts in milliseconds is the violation. If a signal service publishes a setup and you choose to enter, that's discretion. If a bot mirrors fills automatically, that's the prohibited copy pattern.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_8_questi: Does PMT support TPT-specific automation safeguards?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_8_answer: Yes. PickMyTrade has TPT-aware features: per-account contract caps matching the 3/6/9/12/15-mini limits, Trading Time active hours to automatically reject alerts outside your configured window (preventing trades after TPT's EOD cutoff), custom intraday drawdown halts, and weekly P&L distribution smoothing for the consistency check. Configured once, applied to every TradingView webhook.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_9_questi: Is TradingView Pine Script automation allowed?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_9_answer: Yes. Pine Script strategies running on TradingView and firing webhooks via PMT to your TPT Tradovate account are fully allowed. This is the most common TPT automation setup. PickMyTrade processes the webhook, validates per-account risk rules, and submits the order to Tradovate FCM connected to TPT.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_10_quest: What's the safest automation pattern on TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_automation_10_answe: Single TPT PRO Account, your own proprietary TradingView strategy, PMT routing webhooks to Tradovate, Trading Time active hours configured to end before TPT's EOD cutoff. PickMyTrade includes a Trading Time feature available across all supported broker connections. You can configure specific active trading windows with start and end times (24-hour ET format) — any alerts outside those hours are automatically rejected — no new trades are placed. You can set your trading window to end before TPT's EOD cutoff, preventing any new trades from being placed after that time. Full guide: https://docs.pickmytrade.io/docs/trading-time-settings/
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_platforms_title: Which Platforms Does Take Profit Trader Support?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_1_questio: What trading platforms does TPT support?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_1_answer: Three: NinjaTrader (with NT Continuum data), Tradovate (web/desktop), and TradingView via Tradovate connectivity. You pick one platform when activating PRO and can switch with a request to support. Tradovate is the most popular for TradingView automation users; NinjaTrader is preferred by chart-heavy discretionary traders.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_2_answer: Currently no - Rithmic is not natively supported. TPT runs on NinjaTrader Continuum (separate from Rithmic) and Tradovate's own infrastructure. If you need Rithmic for a specific platform, look at Apex, Topstep, or MyFundedFutures, which offer Rithmic connectivity. PMT supports Rithmic on the firms that use it.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_3_questio: Can I use TradingView directly with TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_3_answer: Yes - through Tradovate's broker integration in TradingView. TradingView connects to your TPT-issued Tradovate credentials, displaying TPT account data and accepting orders directly from the chart. Pine Script alerts - webhooks - PMT - Tradovate API - TPT account is the most-used automation flow.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_4_answer: Tradovate web/desktop is free for TPT customers. NinjaTrader requires a license (Lifetime $1,099 or Lease ~$60/month) for advanced features; the free version supports TPT Sim accounts but with charting limitations. TradingView's premium tiers ($14-$60/month) unlock more concurrent webhooks if needed.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_5_questio: Which platform is best for automated trading at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_5_answer: Tradovate via TradingView + PickMyTrade. The webhook flow has low latency (typically under 500ms end-to-end), runs on cloud-hosted PMT infrastructure (no local PC dependency), and supports multi-firm broadcasting. NinjaTrader supports automation natively but requires a local PC running 24/7 - less reliable for set-and-forget systems.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_6_questio: Can I use NinjaScript bots at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_6_answer: Yes - NinjaTrader's native NinjaScript automation runs on TPT NT Continuum accounts. Personal NinjaScript strategies (your own code) are permitted. Mass-distributed NT8 paid bots are subject to the same commercial-bot prohibition. PMT does not directly route to NinjaTrader; for NT users, the platform's own automation is the recommended path.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_7_answer: Yes - Tradovate has iOS and Android apps with full order entry, position monitoring, and chart access. NinjaTrader Mobile is more limited. TradingView mobile app supports order entry to Tradovate. Most disciplined PRO traders avoid mobile-only execution because the trailing drawdown punishes mistimed taps.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_8_questio: What's the latency of PMT webhooks to TPT Tradovate?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_8_answer: Median end-to-end (TradingView fire - PMT process - Tradovate fill confirmation) is 300-700ms. PMT runs cloud infrastructure colocated near major exchange data centers. For most discretionary and swing automation strategies this is fast enough; ultra-HFT styles aren't TPT-permitted anyway.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_9_answer: Yes. Submit a support ticket to switch from NinjaTrader to Tradovate or vice versa. Account history transfers; only the platform UI changes. Often takes 24-48 hours to provision new credentials. Some traders switch from NT to Tradovate specifically to add TradingView/PMT automation.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_10_questi: How do I connect PMT to my TPT Tradovate account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_platforms_10_answer: Go to pickmytrade.trade, add Tradovate as your broker connection, and authenticate with your TPT-issued Tradovate credentials. Then use Generate Alert to get your JSON configuration and webhook URL. Paste the webhook URL into your TradingView alert and the JSON into the alert message. PMT validates the connection in 2-3 minutes. Full setup guide: https://docs.pickmytrade.trade/docs/automating-tradingview-strategies-with-pickmytrade/
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_reset_title: How Do Take Profit Trader Resets, Refunds, and Account Closures Work?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_1_question: How much does a Test phase reset cost?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_1_answer: $100 flat for any Test phase size, AND one free reset is included with each monthly subscription renewal. Reset clears the failed trailing drawdown, sets your balance back to starting capital, and you continue under the existing monthly subscription. Cheaper than purchasing a new Test. PRO resets are separate (size-scaled, $449-$1,499, max 3).
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_2_question: How many times can I reset the Test or PRO?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_2_answer: Test phase: unlimited paid resets at $100 flat, plus one free reset with each monthly renewal. PRO: up to 3 paid resets per account, with size-scaled fees from roughly $449 (smaller sizes) to $1,499 (larger sizes). PRO+ live brokerage accounts cannot typically be reset - breaches are terminal and you’d need to repurchase a Test.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_3_answer: Subscription fees are non-refundable once the Test phase starts trading. The PRO Account activation fee is non-refundable once paid. Reset fees are non-refundable. Cancellation simply stops future renewal charges. TPT does occasionally honor refund requests for technical glitches caused on their side; submit a support ticket with documentation.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_4_question: Can I cancel my TPT subscription anytime?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_4_answer: Yes. Log into the dashboard, go to billing, click cancel. The active month continues until the renewal date; no new charge after that. You retain access through the current billing cycle. PRO and PRO+ accounts don't have a subscription - they only require trading activity to remain active.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_5_question: What happens if I let my Test subscription lapse?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_5_answer: The Test phase account closes when the subscription expires. Any progress (current balance, trailing drawdown level, days traded toward the 5-day minimum) is lost. To resume, purchase a fresh Test - old progress does not carry forward. Always renew or cancel intentionally; don't let it lapse mid-pass.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_6_question: Can I pause my Test phase?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_6_answer: No formal pause feature. Cancel and resubscribe later if needed, but progress resets. The closest thing to "pause" is to simply stop trading - your account remains active without orders. The trailing drawdown won't move because there's no activity, so you can step away for days or weeks within an active billing month.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_7_question: What happens to my PRO Account if I stop trading?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_7_answer: PRO and PRO+ accounts have a minimum activity expectation: typically one trade every 30 days. Beyond that, the account may be marked inactive and closed. If closed, accumulated unrequested profits are forfeited. Always request payouts before extended absences and place at least one small trade per month to maintain status.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_8_question: If I fail PRO, can I get a discount on my next Test?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_reset_8_answer: Sometimes - TPT runs occasional "comeback" promotions for previously funded traders, with discount codes ranging from 25% to 50% off the next Test phase. Check email for re-engagement offers. There's no guaranteed reduced-price re-entry; pricing reverts to standard list/promo for new Test purchases.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_compare_title: How Does Take Profit Trader Compare to Other Prop Firms?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_1_question: Take Profit Trader vs Apex Trader Funding - which is better?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_1_answer: TPT wins on payout cadence (on-demand vs Apex 8-day) and uniquely offers PRO+ - a real LIVE Tradovate brokerage tier with a flat 90/10 split. Apex wins on size variety (up to $300K), instant funded option, and looser copy-trade rules historically. PRO at TPT pays a flat 80/20; PRO+ flat 90/10. Pick TPT for live-execution upgrade path; Apex for larger sim sizes.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_2_question: Take Profit Trader vs Topstep - which is better?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_2_answer: Topstep enforces a Max Loss Limit per day; TPT does not. Topstep pays monthly; TPT pays on-demand. Topstep is the OG (founded 2012) with the strongest brand and broadest education. TPT’s 3-tier model (Test → PRO sim → PRO+ live) is unique among major US futures props. Pick Topstep for structured risk safeguards and education; TPT for on-demand payouts and the live-brokerage upgrade.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_3_answer: MFFU offers more plan variety (Core, Rapid, Pro, Builder, Flex) and bigger sizes (up to $300K). TPT is simpler - one Test phase, five sizes, plus PRO and PRO+ tiers. MFFU’s static drawdown option is friendlier than TPT’s intraday trailing on PRO. TPT’s PRO+ live-brokerage tier (flat 90/10) is something MFFU does not offer. TPT for the live upgrade path; MFFU for plan variety.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_4_answer: Bulenox runs aggressive 1-step like TPT but with looser trailing drawdowns and a simpler split (90% from dollar one on funded). Bulenox uses Rithmic (not Tradovate) — different platform stack from TPT. Many multi-firm traders run Bulenox alongside TPT to diversify. Bulenox does not offer a live-brokerage tier — TPT’s PRO+ is unique in that regard.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_5_answer: FundedNext is primarily forex with a smaller futures arm. TPT is futures-only and more mature in the futures vertical. For pure futures traders, TPT is the better fit. For traders mixing forex and futures, FundedNext or E8 Markets makes more sense. Don't pick FundedNext for futures-only - TPT's product is more refined for the asset class.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_6_question: Should I run TPT alongside other prop firms with PMT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_6_answer: Yes - multi-firm broadcasting is the most common advanced PMT use case. One TradingView Pine strategy fires a single webhook; PMT routes copies to TPT, Apex, MFFU, Topstep, and Bulenox simultaneously. Diversifies firm-specific risk (rule changes, outages, account closures). Single $50/month per broker connection covers every connected firm including TPT’s PRO+ live brokerage.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_7_question: Is TPT cheaper than Apex over a 6-month period?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_7_answer: Depends on pass speed. TPT's monthly Test subscription means each month adds cost; Apex charges one eval fee then monthly funded fee. If you pass TPT in 1 month and quickly graduate to PRO and PRO+ (no recurring fee), TPT is cheaper. If it takes 4-6 months on the Test phase, Apex's structure starts to win. Promo codes affect both. Math out per-pass cost based on your historical timeline.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_8_question: What's the multi-firm playbook on PMT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_8_answer: Common stack: 1 TPT 50 (Test → PRO → PRO+), 1 Apex 50K, 1 MFFU 50K, 1 Topstep 50K. Same TradingView Pine strategy, single webhook, PMT broadcasts. ~$1,000/month combined Test/eval subscription cost while in evaluation; potential combined on-demand payouts of $1,500-$3,000 once all four funded accounts are active. Diversifies firm-specific failure modes. Don't run identical fills across the same firm - that's the copy-trade violation.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_9_question: Do I owe taxes on TPT profits?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_9_answer: Yes - taxable income wherever you live. TPT issues a 1099-NEC for US traders (self-employment income on PRO; live brokerage income on PRO+). International traders receive payment statements via PayPal/Wise/Plaid. UK: HMRC self-employment. India: ITR-3 business income. EU: per-country trading income. Consult a local tax professional.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_10_question: Where can I see TPT payout proof?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_10_answer: TPT's official X (Twitter), Discord, YouTube channel, plus payout-proof posts on prop firm forums, futures trader forums, and day trader forums. Trustpilot has roughly 8,751 reviews referencing payouts at ~4.4/5. Cross-reference firm-published numbers with community user reports for the truest picture. PMT users frequently share on-demand payout receipts from both PRO and PRO+ accounts.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_11_question: Can I trade TPT on a VPS?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_11_answer: Yes. NinjaTrader on a Windows VPS is permitted and common for traders running NinjaScript automation 24/7. Tradovate runs in-browser, also VPS-compatible. PickMyTrade is cloud-hosted, eliminating the VPS need for TradingView automation users - webhooks fire from PMT's infrastructure even when your local PC is off.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_12_question: TPT vs TickTickTrader - which suits algo traders better?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_12_answer: TickTickTrader is newer with explicit algo-friendly messaging and ProjectX/Tradovate platform support. TPT has more brand maturity and on-demand payouts that beat TickTick’s 14-day cycle. For automation-first traders, both work via PMT. TPT’s PRO uses an intraday trailing drawdown that’s stricter than TickTick’s static-drawdown options, but TPT’s PRO+ live brokerage tier is something TickTick does not offer. Most multi-firm PMT users run both side by side.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_13_question: Final pick - should I start with TPT in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_13_answer: If you want a 1-step Test, on-demand payouts, no daily loss limit, and the unique option to graduate to a real LIVE Tradovate brokerage (PRO+ at 90/10) — yes, TPT is one of the best options. Pair it with PickMyTrade for TradingView automation and you’re set up for $50/month per broker connection across TPT and any future firm additions. Start at TPT 50, learn the Test rules, push toward PRO and PRO+.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_14_question: Can I set trading time restrictions in PickMyTrade for my TPT account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_compare_14_answer: PickMyTrade includes a Trading Time feature available across all supported broker connections. You can configure specific active trading windows with start and end times (24-hour ET format). Any TradingView alerts received outside your configured hours are automatically rejected — no new trades are placed. Existing open positions remain active. Settings can be applied to specific accounts or all accounts at once. Full guide: https://docs.pickmytrade.io/docs/trading-time-settings/ For Tradovate connections, PickMyTrade also integrates with ForexFactory to automatically pause trading before and after scheduled news events — it can close open positions and cancel pending limit/stop orders during news windows. Tradovate Trading Time guide: https://docs.pickmytrade.trade/docs/trading-time-settings/
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cat_gap_tpt_title: What's New for Take Profit Trader Tax, KYC, and PRO+ Rules?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_1_question: Does Take Profit Trader send a 1099 tax form, and which form do international traders fill out?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_1_answer: Yes. US-based funded traders complete a W-9 and receive a Form 1099 from TPT once yearly payouts cross the IRS reporting threshold, since payouts are treated as independent-contractor income rather than capital gains. International traders instead submit a W-8BEN to certify non-US status, and TPT generally does not issue them a 1099 — you are responsible for declaring the income under your own country's tax rules. Both forms are completed inside the payout flow before your first withdrawal, so set this up early to avoid delays. Always verify current requirements on TPT's official site.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_2_question: What documents does TPT's KYC check require, and how long does verification take?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_2_answer: TPT runs KYC through a third-party identity provider when you activate a funded account, requiring a government photo ID, a proof-of-address document, and a phone number. Most checks clear automatically within minutes; anything routed to manual review is typically resolved within 24-48 hours during business days. Your registered legal name must match the name on your chosen payout method, or the withdrawal can be held for AML review. Confirm the current document list on TPT's official help center, as verification providers and rules change.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_3_question: What exactly happens to my open position at the 5 PM ET end-of-day cutoff?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_3_answer: If you still have a position open at 5 PM ET, TPT auto-liquidates it at market during the CME maintenance window, which is a low-liquidity period where fills can be noticeably worse than the last traded price. The flatten is logged as a rules event, and repeated overnight-hold attempts can flag the account, force a paid reset, or close it depending on phase and severity. The cleanest practice is to set your own auto-flat a few minutes before the cutoff so you control the exit rather than relying on the firm's forced liquidation. Verify the exact cutoff on TPT's official site.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_4_question: How does the PRO buffer (safety net) work before my first withdrawal?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_4_answer: On a PRO account you cannot withdraw until your balance reaches the "buffer," which is your starting balance plus your maximum drawdown amount. For example, on a $50K account with a $2,000 drawdown, you must hit $52,000 before any payout unlocks. Once you clear the buffer you can withdraw at the PRO split, and PRO+ accounts remove the buffer requirement entirely. Always confirm your account's exact buffer figure on TPT's official site, since drawdown amounts vary by size.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_5_question: How do I get promoted from PRO to PRO+, and what changes?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_5_answer: PRO+ is an automatic, performance-based promotion — you don't apply for it. The common path is accumulating roughly $5,000 in profit on your PRO account, after which TPT upgrades qualifying traders. The upgrade swaps the intraday trailing drawdown for an end-of-day drawdown, removes the buffer requirement, and raises your split to 90/10 with day-one withdrawal access. Because the exact promotion criteria are adjusted periodically, verify the current thresholds on TPT's official site.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_6_question: Do I keep 100% of the first $5,000 in profit on a PRO account?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_6_answer: Yes — the first $5,000 of profit you generate on a PRO account is paid out at 100%, with no firm share taken on that portion. After that initial amount, the standard 80/20 PRO split applies (or 90/10 once you're on PRO+). This is separate from the buffer rule, which still governs when withdrawals unlock. Confirm the current first-payout terms on TPT's official site, as split structures change.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_7_question: What are the most common reasons a TPT payout gets delayed or denied?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_7_answer: The frequent causes are a consistency-rule miss (a single day making up too large a share of total profit), not meeting the minimum funded trading days, an unresolved KYC or tax form, or payout details that don't match your registered legal name and trigger an AML hold. Genuine outright denials are uncommon — most "denials" traders report are temporary holds during compliance or weekend review. To avoid this, spread profit across multiple days, finish KYC and your W-9/W-8BEN early, and keep your payout account in your own name. Verify the current consistency threshold on TPT's official site.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_8_question: What's the difference between the trading account, the wallet, and my bank when I withdraw?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_8_answer: TPT uses a two-stage flow: profit is first moved from your trading account into an internal wallet, and you then withdraw from the wallet to your bank or payout provider. The account-to-wallet transfer typically processes within about 24 business hours, and the wallet-to-bank step usually lands within hours to one business day after that. You can request a withdrawal on any day, so the wallet acts as the staging layer between booked profit and cash in hand. Confirm current processing windows on TPT's official site.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_9_question: Is there a withdrawal fee on small TPT payouts?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_9_answer: Withdrawals above $250 are processed with no fee, while small withdrawals of $250 or less carry a $50 processing fee. Because that fee is flat, requesting tiny amounts is inefficient — it's usually better to let profit accumulate and withdraw above the $250 threshold. There's no published maximum cap on how much you can withdraw per request. Verify the current fee schedule on TPT's official site, as thresholds can change.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_10_question: Why am I asked to sign a Market Data Agreement, and which option do I pick?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_10_answer: Before live data streams to your platform, the exchange requires you to sign a Market Data Agreement and declare professional or non-professional status. Most retail funded traders qualify as Non-Professional, so you select that option unless you trade for a firm or manage others' money. After signing the non-pro agreements (and choosing your CQG or Rithmic feed), your TPT dashboard status usually updates within about 10-15 minutes. If your data isn't loading, an unsigned agreement is the most common cause — verify the steps on TPT's official help center.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_11_question: What's the difference between the CQG and Rithmic data feeds at TPT?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_11_answer: TPT offers both CQG and Rithmic market data, and which you use depends on your platform and account setup rather than a quality difference — both are professional-grade futures feeds. Rithmic is commonly paired with NinjaTrader and similar desktop platforms, while Tradovate-based access (the route PickMyTrade automates) uses its own connection. Each feed has its own non-professional agreement to sign during activation. Check TPT's official help center for the feed that matches your chosen platform.
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_12_question: Can I withdraw from my TPT funded account every day?
prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_q_gap_tpt_12_answer: Yes — once you're eligible (buffer cleared on PRO, or immediately on PRO+), TPT allows daily withdrawal requests with no fixed monthly payout day to wait for. There's no published per-day maximum, though each request still passes the consistency check and standard compliance review. In practice many traders still batch withdrawals to stay above the $250 no-fee threshold. Confirm current daily-payout terms on TPT's official site.

prop_firm_faq.take_profit_trader_cta_text: TPT supports Tradovate-connected TradingView automation. PickMyTrade routes Pine Script alerts to your TPT Tradovate account in under 700ms. $50/month flat across all your TPT accounts and any other prop firm you connect.

prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_basics_title: What Is Apex Trader Funding and How Does It Work?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a1: Apex Trader Funding is a US-based futures prop firm founded in 2021 by Darrell Martin (his earlier Apex Investing Institute education business dates to 2008, but Apex Trader Funding itself launched in 2021) and headquartered in Austin, Texas. You pay a one-time evaluation fee, hit a profit target without breaching drawdown rules, and graduate to a Performance Account where Apex pays 100% of the first $25,000 in lifetime profits per PA, then a 90/10 split above that. Apex is the largest US futures prop firm by branded search volume — roughly 135,000 monthly Google searches as of 2026.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q2: Who owns Apex and when was it founded?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a2: Apex Trader Funding was founded in 2021 by Darrell Martin, who remains CEO. Headquartered in Austin, Texas. Note that Martin's earlier company Apex Investing Institute dates back to 2008, but Apex Trader Funding is a separate entity that launched in 2021. The firm is privately held; ownership is concentrated with founding-team investors and not publicly disclosed.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q3: Is Apex Trader Funding legit or a scam in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a3: Apex is legit by every standard prop firm metric — they have paid out hundreds of millions of dollars over the firm's lifetime, hold a Trustpilot rating of roughly 4.4/5 across ~18,000 reviews (May 2026), and have operated continuously since the 2021 launch through the 80+ prop firm collapses of 2024-2025. The 4.0 launch in March 2026 modernized the model further. Common complaints (payout "Under Review" delays, rule confusion, hedging detection) exist but are policy disputes, not scam indicators. Read the funded trader agreement carefully before paying.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q4: How much money has Apex paid out to traders?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a4: Apex publicly cites "hundreds of millions" in lifetime payouts and is consistently in the top 10 industry payout league tables (Q1 2026 saw $115M tracked across the top 10 firms collectively). The exact monthly figure varies but Apex has been one of the largest single payout sources in the futures prop industry for several years.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q5: Is Apex regulated as a broker?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a5: No. Apex is a technology / contractor company that provides simulated trading evaluations and pays winning traders as independent contractors. It is not registered as a broker-dealer or FCM with the SEC, CFTC, or FINRA. The legal relationship is governed by the Apex Funded Trader Agreement, not exchange rules. The CFTC has been increasing scrutiny of retail prop firms in 2024-2026 but no firm-specific regulation has been finalized.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q6: Are Apex accounts real money or simulated?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a6: Evaluations are 100% simulated. Performance Accounts (PA) — the funded phase — are also simulated for most traders, with payouts coming from Apex's challenge revenue. Live Funded Accounts (LFA) are a separate tier where some real capital is involved, accessible by invitation after demonstrating consistency. The vast majority of Apex traders never reach LFA; most run sim -> PA -> payout indefinitely.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q7: Does Apex actually take real positions in the market?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a7: Not on most accounts. Apex aggregates exposure across the trader base and hedges select positions in real markets where their book demands it, but the typical trader's individual orders fill on simulated quotes that mirror real-time market data. LFA traders have real fills.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q8: Why does Apex have mixed Trustpilot reviews?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a8: A few common patterns. Negative reviews concentrate on payout "Under Review" delays during the Legacy 3.0 era (now mostly resolved with 4.0 automated payouts via ACH, Wise, Plane, and crypto rails), the June 12 2025 connection outage where Apex did not reverse losses, and rule misreadings (especially trailing drawdown shock and consistency rule). Positive reviews focus on actual payouts received, the 4.0 rule improvements, and customer support response time. The 4.0 model removed the biggest historical pain points — overall Trustpilot sits at roughly 4.4/5 across ~18,000 reviews (May 2026).
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q9: Where can I see real Apex payout proof?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a9: Apex publishes a payouts page at apextraderfunding.com/payouts/ with live and lifetime figures. Independent verification on prop firm forums, Trustpilot, and trader Discord servers shows consistent payout patterns. Affiliate review sites (ProTradingVibes, BestPropFirms, TradersSecondBrain) also aggregate community payout reports. Always cross-reference Apex's claimed figures with community proofs before trusting headline numbers.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a10: Darrell Martin is the founder and CEO of Apex Trader Funding. He has a long background in retail futures trading and education prior to founding Apex; his face appears prominently on Apex marketing and educational content. Active on YouTube and Apex social channels.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_v4_title: What Changed Between Apex 4.0 and the Legacy 3.0 Rules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a11: Apex 4.0 is the new product version launched March 1, 2026 — the biggest restructure in Apex's history. It replaced monthly subscriptions with one-time fees, eliminated the MAE rule, removed the 5:1 risk-reward rule on evaluations, removed the One-Direction rule, dropped the Legacy 8-day minimum trading-day requirement to 5 days between payouts, automated payouts via ACH/Wise/Plane/crypto rails, and relaxed consistency from 30% to 50%. Existing Legacy 3.0 accounts keep their old rules; new accounts are 4.0 by default.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a12: March 1, 2026. Every new evaluation purchased on or after that date runs on 4.0 rules. Accounts purchased before March 1, 2026 are Legacy 3.0 and stay on the original rule set unless you choose to migrate.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q13: What's the difference between Apex 3.0 and 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a13: 4.0 changes vs 3.0: monthly subscription removed (now one-time eval fee + one-time PA activation fee); MAE rule removed; 5:1 risk-reward rule on eval removed; One-Direction rule removed; minimum trading days between payouts dropped from 8 (Legacy) to 5 (4.0); consistency rule relaxed from 30% to 50%; payouts automated through ACH/Wise/Plane/crypto rails (no more "Under Review" delays); evaluation has a hard 30 calendar day window (no resets); PA must be activated within 7 days of passing; $75K, $250K, and $300K plans removed from the new 4.0 lineup (current 4.0 sizes are $25K / $50K / $100K / $150K). Legacy 3.0 accounts still operate under the old rules.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q14: Are my old Legacy / 3.0 accounts still active under old rules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a14: Yes. Legacy 3.0 accounts keep all their original rules — MAE, 5:1 RR, One-Direction, 30% consistency, 8-day minimum between payouts, monthly subscription. Nothing about 4.0 was retroactive. The two product versions run side by side, which is why double-checking which version your account is on matters.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q15: Will Apex force me to migrate my Legacy account to 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a15: No forced migration as of April 2026. Apex has indicated Legacy accounts will continue to operate indefinitely on 3.0 rules. If you want 4.0 rules, you have to purchase a new evaluation under the 4.0 model — your existing 3.0 account is not auto-converted.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q16: Did Apex remove the MAE rule?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a16: Yes, in 4.0. The Maximum Adverse Excursion (MAE) rule — which capped open-trade unrealized loss at a percentage of the daily target — was eliminated entirely. Legacy 3.0 accounts still have it.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q17: Did Apex remove the 5:1 risk-reward rule?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a17: Yes, on 4.0 evaluations. The 5:1 rule (no single trade can risk more than 1/5 of daily realized profit at any point) was removed. Legacy 3.0 evaluations still enforce it.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q18: Did Apex remove the One-Direction rule?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a18: Yes in 4.0. The One-Direction rule that restricted same-instrument long and short simultaneously was removed. Hedging across multiple Apex accounts is still banned, but within-account opposite directions are now permitted on 4.0.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q19: Did Apex remove the minimum-trading-days-between-payouts requirement?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a19: Reduced, not eliminated. Apex 4.0 requires 5 qualifying trading days between payouts (down from Legacy 3.0's 8-day minimum). Legacy 3.0 accounts still operate under the original 8-day rule.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q20: Did Apex stop charging monthly subscription fees?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a20: Yes on 4.0. The monthly $85 (or similar) subscription is gone — replaced by a one-time evaluation fee plus a one-time PA activation fee ($79 Intraday or $99 EOD). Legacy 3.0 accounts still bill monthly until they end.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q21: Are 4.0 evaluations harder or easier than Legacy?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a21: Easier overall for most traders. The relaxed consistency rule (30% to 50%), removed MAE/5:1/One-Direction rules, and 5-day between-payout minimum (vs Legacy's 8) all reduce friction. The 30 calendar day hard limit on evaluations is the one tightening — there are no resets in 4.0, so if you can't pass in 30 days, you have to buy a new evaluation. For traders who pass quickly, 4.0 is a clear win; for traders who need multiple resets, the math is more nuanced.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q22: How do I tell if my account is 3.0 or 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a22: Check the purchase date in your dashboard. Anything purchased before March 1, 2026 is Legacy 3.0; anything on or after is 4.0. The dashboard also displays the rule set tied to each account; if you see references to MAE, 5:1, or One-Direction, you are on Legacy. If you see "50% consistency" and no MAE references, you are on 4.0.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_account_types_title: What Are the Apex Account Types — Eval, PA, and LFA?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q23: What's the difference between Evaluation Account and Performance Account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a23: Evaluation is the test phase — you must hit the profit target without breaching drawdown. Performance Account (PA) is the funded phase you graduate into, where there is no profit target and you can request payouts. PA rules are slightly looser (no profit target requirement), but the trailing drawdown still applies, plus the consistency rule and minimum-day rules for first payout. The PA is where you actually make money.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q24: Is the Performance Account real or simulated?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a24: Simulated. Apex pays real cash for PA performance, but the underlying account is sim — your orders fill against simulated quotes that mirror real market data. This is the standard model for almost all retail futures props.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q25: What is a Live Funded Account (LFA) at Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a25: Live Funded Account is Apex's tier where real capital is in play. It is invitation-only, granted to PA traders who have demonstrated consistent payouts over time. LFA rules are different: no trailing drawdown (only daily loss limit), no consistency rule, real exchange fills. Most Apex traders never reach LFA — and the path is opaque.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q26: How do I get invited to a Live Funded Account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a26: Apex doesn't publish exact criteria. Generally requires multiple successful payouts on a PA, demonstrated low-volatility profitability, KYC complete, no rule violations. The invitation is at Apex's discretion. Plan to live on PA indefinitely — LFA is a bonus, not a guaranteed outcome.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q27: Does Apex offer one-step or two-step evaluations?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a27: One-step. You hit the profit target without breaching drawdown, then you graduate to PA. There is no separate phase 2 verification.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q28: Can I skip the evaluation and go straight to a PA?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a28: No. Apex does not offer instant funding. You must pass an evaluation to access a PA.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q29: Once I pass the eval, how long until I get my PA?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a29: PA activation is typically immediate after you pay the activation fee ($79 Intraday or $99 EOD on 4.0). You have 7 calendar days from passing the eval to activate; miss the window and the pass expires. Once activated, the PA goes live within hours.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q30: What happens if I don't activate my PA within 7 days?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a30: The pass expires and you lose access to that PA opportunity. You'd have to buy a new evaluation and start over. Set a reminder — the 7-day window catches a lot of traders, especially those who pass on a Friday and forget over the weekend.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q31: Do I have to pay a monthly fee on a PA in 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a31: No. Apex 4.0 PAs have a one-time activation fee only — no recurring monthly subscription. Legacy 3.0 PAs still bill monthly.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a32: PAs do not have a hard expiration but can go inactive. Apex enforces an inactivity rule — no trades for 30+ days flags the account; longer inactivity may close it. Trade at least once a month to keep the PA active.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q33: Can I run multiple PAs at the same time?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a33: Yes — up to 20 active PA accounts maximum per individual trader (Apex's 20-cap rule applies per trader, not per household). You can buy multiple evaluations, pass each, and run all the resulting PAs in parallel. Same-direction copy trading across your own accounts is permitted; hedging is not.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q34: How are PA rules different from LFA rules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a34: PA: trailing drawdown applies, consistency rule applies, daily loss limit applies, payouts capped on first 5 then uncapped. LFA: no trailing drawdown (only DLL), no consistency rule, real fills, payouts processed differently. LFA is structurally easier to trade because the trailing drawdown is removed; the path to LFA is the hard part.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_pricing_title: What Account Sizes and Pricing Does Apex Offer?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q35: What account sizes does Apex offer in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a35: Apex 4.0 offers exactly four sizes: $25K, $50K, $100K, and $150K. The $75K plan was retired under 4.0 (it remains a Legacy 3.0 option for existing holders only). The $250K and $300K Legacy plans were also dropped from the 4.0 lineup. Existing Legacy 3.0 holders of $75K, $250K, or $300K accounts retain those — but new buyers cannot acquire them under 4.0.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q36: How much does the $25K Apex eval cost?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a36: List price around $199 one-time on 4.0, frequently 50-90% off with discount codes. Black Friday and seasonal promos push to $20-$40 territory. Verify the live price on apextraderfunding.com — discounts run almost continuously.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q37: How much does the $50K Apex eval cost?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a37: List around $249 one-time on 4.0; with discount codes typically $50-$130 depending on promotion. The $50K is the most popular plan among new traders because it balances eval cost against meaningful contract size.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q38: How much does the $100K Apex eval cost?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a38: List around $399 one-time on 4.0; discounted to $100-$220 typical. Recommended for traders who specifically want full-size ES/NQ access (the $25K and $50K plans are usually micros-only).
