prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q39: How much does the $150K Apex eval cost?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a39: List around $599 one-time on 4.0; discounted to $200-$350 typical. The largest 4.0 plan available; the $250K and $300K Legacy plans were retired.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q40: Did Apex remove the $250K and $300K plans in 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a40: Yes — the $250K and $300K plans are not available on the 4.0 product. Existing Legacy 3.0 holders of those accounts retain access to them; new buyers can only go up to $150K under 4.0.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a41: $99 one-time on 4.0 for EOD trailing drawdown plans. Paid after passing the evaluation, before the PA activates.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a42: $79 one-time on 4.0 for Intraday trailing drawdown plans. Cheaper than the EOD activation fee because Intraday accounts are riskier to trade.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q43: Why is the EOD account more expensive than the Intraday?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a43: Because EOD trailing drawdown is dramatically friendlier to the trader — your trail only updates at the close of each day, so intraday wicks don't kill the account. Apex prices the EOD activation higher because more traders pass and reach payout on EOD plans, so Apex needs more revenue per account to balance the economics.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q44: Is the activation fee a one-time charge or recurring?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a44: One-time on 4.0. Pay it once when you activate your PA; no recurring billing. Legacy 3.0 has different mechanics where the monthly subscription continues.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q45: Does Apex still bill monthly under 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a45: No. Apex 4.0 eliminated monthly billing entirely. You pay the eval fee once, then the activation fee once when you pass — no recurring charges. Legacy 3.0 accounts still bill monthly until terminated.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q46: Does Apex accept crypto / PayPal / credit cards?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a46: Major credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, Amex) are the primary payment methods. PayPal availability varies. Crypto for evaluation purchase is not standard. Apex does pay OUT in crypto (and via ACH, Wise, or Plane) for international traders, but inbound payments are typically card-based.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_discount_title: Are There Apex Discount Codes or Promotions?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q47: What's the current Apex discount code in April 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a47: Apex publishes active codes at apextraderfunding.com/coupon-code/ — they rotate frequently. Affiliate aggregators (SaveOnPropFirms, ProTradingVibes, BestPropFirms) also list current codes. Always pull the live code from one of those sources at purchase time; codes expire weekly.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q48: How often does Apex run discount promos?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a48: Almost continuously. There is rarely a week without an active promo code. Major events (Black Friday, Cyber Monday, Memorial Day, Easter, July 4th, anniversary of Apex's founding) push deeper discounts — often 80%+ off list. Patient traders never pay list price.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q49: What's the maximum discount Apex offers?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a49: Up to 90% off the list price during major promotions. The headline 90% number requires a flagship promo (Black Friday, anniversary). Day-to-day codes typically run 50-70% off. The realistic effective price for a $50K eval with code stacking is around $50-$130.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q50: Do discount codes apply to PA activation fees?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a50: No. Discount codes apply to evaluation purchases only. The PA activation fee ($79 Intraday or $99 EOD) is fixed and not discounted.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q51: Do discount codes apply to resets?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a51: Apex 4.0 does not have resets — failed evaluations require buying a new evaluation, which can use a discount code. Legacy 3.0 reset purchases sometimes accept codes; varies by promotion.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q52: Can I stack multiple Apex coupon codes?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a52: No. Only one code per checkout. The aggressive "stack two codes for 95% off" claims you see online don't work — checkout rejects the second code.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q53: Where do I find verified discount codes?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a53: Three sources: apextraderfunding.com/coupon-code/ (Apex's own page), Apex's email newsletter (subscribe for the freshest codes), and aggregator sites (SaveOnPropFirms, ProTradingVibes). Avoid random YouTube comment codes — many are stale or affiliate-only.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q54: Does Apex offer a holiday Black Friday deal each year?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a54: Yes, every year. Black Friday and Cyber Monday have historically been Apex's deepest discounts of the year — 80-90% off list across all plan sizes. Apex emails subscribers a few days in advance. If you can wait until late November, the Black Friday eval is the cheapest entry point.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q55: What's the profit target on a $25K eval?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a55: $1,500 net P&L on the standard 4.0 $25K plan. Hit it without breaching trailing drawdown and you've passed the eval. Verify on apextraderfunding.com — Apex occasionally adjusts targets per plan version.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q56: What's the profit target on a $50K eval?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a56: $3,000 net P&L on the standard 4.0 $50K plan. The most popular eval target — accessible with disciplined micro-contract scalping over 5-10 trading days.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q57: Is the $75K plan still available, and what was its profit target?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a57: No — the $75K plan was retired under Apex 4.0 (March 2026). It is only available as a Legacy 3.0 account for existing holders. The historical $75K Legacy profit target was $4,250. New buyers should pick from the current 4.0 sizes: $25K ($1,500 target), $50K ($3,000 target), $100K ($6,000 target), or $150K ($9,000 target).
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q58: What's the profit target on a $100K eval?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a58: $6,000 on the standard 4.0 $100K plan. The plan size where full-size ES/NQ trading becomes practical given the larger drawdown buffer.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q59: What's the profit target on a $150K eval?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a59: $9,000 on the standard 4.0 $150K plan — the largest 4.0 size available.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q60: Do profit targets exist on PA accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a60: No. PAs have no profit target. The targets are eval-only. On the PA you focus on hitting payout-eligible thresholds (consistency, qualifying days, minimum profit cushion) rather than a target.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q61: Can I exceed the profit target before passing?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a61: Yes — there is no upper cap. You can hit a $3,000 target and finish at $5,000. Watch the consistency rule though: a single huge day can lock you into needing more days to balance the percentage at PA payout time.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q62: Does the profit target round up or down with floating P&L?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a62: The eval evaluates target hit on closing balance, not floating equity. So you have to actually close trades to bank the profit. Floating $3,500 with a $3,000 target doesn't pass — close the position and watch the closing balance hit $3,000+ to lock the pass.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q63: What happens if I hit the profit target on day 1?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a63: On Apex 4.0, you've passed — there is no minimum trading day requirement on evaluation. The 5-day minimum applies to PA payout eligibility, not eval pass. Hit target day 1, pay activation fee, start the PA, then grind the 5 qualifying days for first payout.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q64: Can I take payouts during evaluation?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a64: No. Payouts are PA-only. The eval is a test — there is no payout mechanism on it. Pass the eval, activate the PA, then earn payouts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_drawdown_title: How Do Apex's Trailing and Daily Drawdown Rules Work?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a65: A maximum loss floor that ratchets up with your peak balance but never decreases. On a $50K Intraday account with $2,500 trailing drawdown, the starting floor is $47,500. Hit a peak of $52,000 and the floor moves to $49,500. Touch the floor and the account dies.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q66: How is intraday trailing drawdown calculated tick by tick?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a66: On Intraday plans, every tick of unrealized profit raises the floor. So if you go from $50,000 starting balance to $51,500 unrealized peak (without closing), the floor moves to $49,000. If price then retraces $2,500 against the open position, the floor is breached even though you haven't closed the trade. Intraday trailing punishes you for "holding through the breath" — close trades to lock balance progress against the trail.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q67: Does the trailing drawdown move on unrealized profit?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a67: Intraday: yes — every tick of unrealized profit moves the floor up. EOD: no — only closing balance moves the floor. This single difference is why most Apex traders pick EOD plans (the $99 activation fee is worth it for the dramatically friendlier mechanics).
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q68: Does intraday trailing drawdown reset overnight?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a68: No — it never resets and never moves down. Once the floor ratchets up, it stays at that level until the freeze condition is met (starting balance + drawdown + $100). Many new traders assume the trail resets at midnight; it does not.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q69: How does Apex's EOD drawdown work, and can my balance dip below it during the day?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a69: No, it cannot dip below it. Apex recalculates the EOD threshold once per trading day at 4:59:59 PM ET from your closing balance, and it only moves up. It is "enforced in real time": if your balance touches or falls below it at any moment, positions are liquidated and the evaluation fails or the PA closes. On a 50K account with $2,000 drawdown, a $50,800 close moves the threshold to $48,800. On PAs it stops trailing at starting balance plus $100. Intraday trailing accounts differ: that threshold trails the highest intraday balance.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q70: Intraday vs EOD — which should I pick?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a70: EOD for almost all traders. The $20 extra activation fee ($99 vs $79) is the cheapest insurance you'll buy in trading. EOD lets you ride bigger trades without fearing intraday wicks killing the account. Pick Intraday only if you have a strategy that closes every trade quickly and never lets unrealized profit drift — and even then, EOD is usually still the better choice.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q71: When does the trailing drawdown stop trailing?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a71: Apex locks the trail at "starting balance + $100." So on a $50K account, once your peak balance hits $52,600 ($50K starting + $2,500 drawdown + $100 buffer), the floor freezes at $50,100 and stops trailing. From that point forward, you have a static drawdown of $50,100. Reaching the freeze threshold is a major Apex milestone — your account is structurally safer afterward.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q72: What happens when my account hits the trailing threshold?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a72: The account is breached. Open positions are auto-liquidated. The account is closed and cannot be reset under 4.0 — you would have to buy a new evaluation. Legacy 3.0 accounts can sometimes use a paid reset.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q73: Are open positions auto-liquidated at the threshold?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a73: Yes. The platform (Tradovate / Rithmic / NinjaTrader) auto-flattens positions the moment the trailing drawdown is breached. There's no human in the loop and no override.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q74: What's the trailing drawdown amount on a $25K account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a74: $1,500 on the 4.0 $25K plan. Tight relative to position size — most $25K traders run micros only.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q75: What's the trailing drawdown amount on a $50K account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a75: $2,500 on the 4.0 $50K plan. Workable for micro contract scalping with 1-2 contract risk.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q76: What's the trailing drawdown amount on a $100K account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a76: $3,000 on the 4.0 $100K plan. Roomier; allows full-size ES/NQ at 1 contract risk.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q77: What's the trailing drawdown amount on a $150K account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a77: $5,000 on the 4.0 $150K plan. The most flexible 4.0 size — comfortable margin for swing-style intraday holds.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q78: What happens when I hit the daily loss limit?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a78: Open positions auto-liquidate, you are paused for the rest of that trading day, and you come back tomorrow. Hitting the DLL does not fail the account — it just suspends trading until 6:00 PM ET (the CME daily reset).
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q79: Does the trailing drawdown apply to Live (LFA) accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a79: No. LFA accounts have only the daily loss limit, not the trailing drawdown. This is a major reason traders work toward LFA — the rule structure is significantly easier once you're there.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q80: Why did my drawdown move when my open position was profitable but I hadn't closed?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a80: You're on an Intraday account. Every tick of unrealized profit moves the floor up — that's the defining behavior of Intraday. Then if price retraces, the elevated floor catches you. The fix is either close trades sooner to lock balance, or switch to EOD on your next account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q81: What is the consistency rule on Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a81: Your single largest profit day cannot exceed a percentage of your total cumulative profit at payout time. Apex 4.0 = 50%. Legacy 3.0 = 30%. So at 50%, if your total profit is $10,000, your best day can be at most $5,000. The rule applies at PA payout request, not during evaluation.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q82: Did the consistency rule change in 4.0?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a82: Yes — relaxed from 30% (Legacy 3.0) to 50% (4.0). This is one of the biggest reasons traders prefer 4.0 to Legacy. A 50% rule needs much less padding from small days to qualify a big day for payout.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q83: How is the consistency rule calculated?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a83: Best single day's net P&L divided by total cumulative net P&L, multiplied by 100. To stay under 50%, total profit must be at least best day / 0.50. So a $2,000 best day requires at least $4,000 total before payout. Use Apex's payout calculator or fundedmath.com to check before requesting.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q84: Does the consistency rule apply during evaluation?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a84: No on Apex 4.0 — eval has no consistency requirement. The rule only applies at PA payout. You can have a single huge day on the eval and still pass; it just may make the first PA payout harder.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q85: Does going over the consistency threshold fail my account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a85: No — it just blocks the payout. The account survives. Trade more small profitable days to dilute the best-day percentage, then re-request the payout. This is the most-misunderstood rule on prop firm forums.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q86: How do I bring my consistency back under 50%?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a86: Trade more small winning days. Every additional profitable day adds to the total denominator and lowers the percentage. Some traders deliberately log $50-100 days for a week after a big day to balance the ratio.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q87: Does the consistency rule reset after a payout?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a87: Yes — the consistency clock resets after each approved payout. The next cycle starts fresh.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q88: Does the consistency rule ever stop applying after enough payouts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a88: The 50% consistency rule does NOT permanently disappear at any payout count — that is a common myth. What changes is the payout cap: after 5 successful payouts on the same PA, the trader becomes eligible to request 100% withdrawal of available profits (caps are lifted on payout #6 onward). But the underlying 50% best-day rule still gates whether a given payout is approved. Track-record traders enjoy bigger checks, not a rule exemption.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q89: Does the 30% rule still apply on Legacy 3.0 accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a89: Yes. Legacy 3.0 PAs still enforce the 30% consistency rule. The 50% relaxation only applies to 4.0 accounts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q90: Is there a tool to calculate my Apex consistency?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a90: fundedmath.com has an Apex consistency calculator. Apex's own dashboard also shows the percentage. Both are useful before clicking "request payout" — knowing you'll be denied saves the support ticket.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_days_title: What Are Apex's Trading Days, Hours, and Holiday Rules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q91: What is a "qualifying day" on Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a91: A trading day where you generated at least the minimum profit threshold (typically $50 net on a $25K, scaling up by account size). Token trades that don't meet the threshold don't count. The 5 qualifying days for first payout (4.0) must all individually meet the minimum.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q92: How many qualifying days do I need for first payout?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a92: 5 qualifying days on Apex 4.0 (down from 7 on Legacy). The days don't need to be consecutive, but each must hit the minimum profit threshold for that account size.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q93: Does the minimum profit per qualifying day vary by account size?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a93: Yes — scales with account size. Roughly $50 minimum on a $25K, $100 on $50K, $200 on $100K, $300 on $150K. Verify exact thresholds in your dashboard for the specific account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q94: Do qualifying days have to be consecutive?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a94: No. The 5 qualifying days can be spread across as long as you want, with non-trading days in between. As long as you eventually log 5 days that each meet the profit minimum, the count progresses.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a95: CME trading hours: 6:00 PM ET Sunday open through 4:59 PM ET Friday close, with daily breaks at 5:00-6:00 PM ET. Apex auto-flattens positions at 4:59 PM ET each day. Sunday open at 6:00 PM ET is the start of a new trading week.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q96: What time must positions be closed daily?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a96: 4:59 PM ET. Apex auto-flattens any open positions at this time across all accounts and platforms. Anything still open at 4:59 gets liquidated at the closing price — sometimes with bad fills if the market is moving.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q97: Can I hold positions overnight at Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a97: No. Apex auto-flattens at 4:59 PM ET every day. There is no swing or overnight account option.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q98: When does the trading day reset?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a98: 6:00 PM ET. After the 5:00-6:00 PM CME maintenance break, the next trading day begins. Daily loss limit resets here, not at midnight. Many new traders trip up by treating midnight as the day boundary; it's not.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q99: Are weekends and holidays considered trading days?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a99: Saturdays no — CME is closed. Holidays generally no — markets close. Sunday opens at 6 PM ET so Sunday evening can technically count as the start of Monday's trading day for daily counting purposes.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q100: Does Apex support trading during CME holiday schedules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a100: Yes — whenever CME is open, Apex accounts can trade. Holiday early-close days (like the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve) follow CME's schedule. Apex's auto-flatten time adjusts to match CME's early close.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_sltp_title: Does Apex Require a Stop-Loss and Take-Profit on Every Trade?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q101: Did Apex really make stop-loss mandatory in March 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a101: Yes. As of March 2026, every order on an Apex account must have an attached stop-loss and take-profit. The platform layer (Tradovate, Rithmic) enforces this — orders without SL/TP are rejected at submission.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q102: Does every order need both an SL and a TP attached?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a102: Yes. Both required. Single-sided orders (just SL or just TP) are rejected. Apex requires bracketed orders — entry + stop + target — for every position.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q103: Will Tradovate reject my order without SL/TP?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a103: Yes. Tradovate's order entry rejects unbracketed orders on Apex accounts as of March 2026. The error message references the SL/TP requirement. Same on Rithmic and NinjaTrader. Note: Apex does not run on ProjectX — ProjectX went Topstep-exclusive in February 2026.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q104: Will Rithmic reject my order without SL/TP?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a104: Yes — same enforcement on Rithmic. Apex's rule applies to the account, not the platform.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q105: How does this affect manual entries?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a105: You have to use the platform's bracket-order interface for every entry. Tradovate has bracket orders built in; Rithmic does too. Discretionary scalpers who used to fire one-click entries now have to set SL/TP at the same moment — slower and requires planning before the click.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q106: How does this affect TradingView alerts and webhooks?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a106: If your TradingView strategy has stop-loss and take-profit logic defined, PickMyTrade reads those values from the alert and sends them to Apex automatically. Alternatively, if your strategy only handles entry orders (buy/sell signals), you can configure SL and TP directly inside PickMyTrade when generating your alert, your TradingView strategy handles the entries, and PMT handles the exits using the values you configured.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a107: Yes, in two ways. If your TradingView strategy already includes stop-loss and take-profit logic, PMT reads those values from the alert and forwards them to Apex. If your strategy only sends entry signals, you can configure SL and TP directly inside PickMyTrade during alert setup, PMT then applies those exit values to every outgoing order automatically.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q108: What happens if my strategy doesn't define a stop-loss?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a108: If your strategy doesn't define a stop-loss or take-profit, PMT will forward only the entry order (buy/sell) to your Apex broker, which is fine if that's all you need. If you want SL and TP applied to every trade, you can configure them directly in PickMyTrade when setting up your alert. Enter your desired SL and TP values in the PMT alert configuration and they will be applied to all outgoing orders automatically.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_instruments_title: Which Instruments Can You Trade on Apex, and Why Was Metals Trading Halted?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q109: What instruments can I trade on Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a109: CME Group products only — Apex does NOT offer EUREX/DAX or any non-CME exchange. Available: equity index futures from CME (ES, NQ, YM, RTY plus micros MES, MNQ, MYM, M2K), energy from NYMEX (CL, NG plus MCL), rates from CBOT (ZB, ZN, ZF), currency futures from CME (6E, 6B, 6J, 6A), agricultural from CBOT (ZC, ZS, ZW). Metals on COMEX/NYMEX are currently halted (Gold, Silver, Copper, Platinum, Palladium plus all micros).
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q110: Why did Apex halt metals trading in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a110: Apex halted GC, SI, MGC, HG, PL, PA in early 2026 citing extreme volatility and risk-management considerations. The decision was platform-wide — applies to Tradovate, Rithmic, NinjaTrader, and WealthCharts Apex accounts. No public timeline for return.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q111: Are Gold, Silver, Micro Gold banned now?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a111: Yes — GC (Gold), SI (Silver), MGC (Micro Gold), QO (Mini Gold), QI (Mini Silver) are all halted. The halt covers full-size and micro contracts equally. Many Apex traders specialized in MGC scalping and had to migrate strategies to other instruments.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q112: Are Copper, Platinum, Palladium also halted?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a112: Yes — HG (Copper), PL (Platinum), PA (Palladium) are also halted along with Gold/Silver. The full metals complex is suspended.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q113: When will metals come back to Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a113: No public timeline as of April 2026. Apex stated they're reviewing quarterly. Watch the Apex announcements page or X account for updates.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q114: Does the metals halt apply to LFA accounts too?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a114: Yes — the halt is firm-wide across Eval, PA, and LFA accounts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q115: What are the most popular instruments to trade on Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a115: MES (Micro E-mini S&P) and MNQ (Micro E-mini Nasdaq) dominate by trader count, especially on $25K and $50K accounts. ES and NQ get more volume on $100K+ plans. CL (crude oil) is popular for trend-following. With metals halted, traders have shifted toward MES, MNQ, and CL.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a116: Yes — ZC (corn), ZS (soybeans), ZW (wheat) are tradable. Volume is lower than equity index futures, but they trade.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q117: Does Apex allow crypto futures (BTC, ETH)?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a117: Limited. Bitcoin micro futures (MBT) availability varies by account size and platform; full-size BTC futures are typically not allowed on smaller plans due to tick value. Verify your specific account's instrument list in Apex's dashboard.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q118: Are micro futures available on every plan?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a118: Yes — micros are universally available across all Apex plan sizes. They're the primary instrument for $25K and $50K traders.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_hedging_title: Does Apex Allow Hedging, Copy Trading, and Multiple Accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a119: Cross-account hedging is universally banned (long on one Apex account, short same instrument on another). Within-account opposite directions are now allowed on Apex 4.0 (the One-Direction rule was removed); Legacy 3.0 still prohibits it.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q120: Does the hedging rule apply across multiple accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a120: Yes — strictly enforced. Holding ES long on one Apex account while holding ES short on another is detected (sub-second order timing across IPs and device fingerprints) and triggers immediate account closure plus payout forfeiture. Apex shares blacklist data with other major futures props.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q121: Is long NQ and short MNQ hedging at Apex, even if the positions are on different accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a121: Yes. Apex's Prohibited Activities page bans "holding both long and short positions simultaneously on the same or correlated instrument," so long NQ against short MNQ counts. For PAs, its copy-trading rule says accounts must "not hedge against correlated assets," and for evaluations Apex says you "may not pass Evaluation Accounts by hedging them against each other." Apex does not publish a list of correlated instruments, so treat products that usually move together as correlated. On an EOD PA, hedging violations "will result in immediate account closure."
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q122: How many Apex PA accounts can I have?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a122: 20 active PA accounts maximum per individual trader (Apex's 20-cap is per-trader, not per-household — a common misreading). The cap counts across all platforms (Tradovate + Rithmic + NinjaTrader + WealthCharts). Buy more than 20 evals and pass them, you can hold the additional ones inactive but only 20 can be active simultaneously.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q123: Does the 20-cap apply across Tradovate, Rithmic, and NinjaTrader?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a123: Yes — 20 across all platforms combined, not 20 per platform. So 10 Tradovate PAs + 10 Rithmic PAs hits the cap.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q124: Can my spouse have separate Apex accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a124: Yes — your spouse can hold their own separate set of up to 20 PA accounts as an independent individual trader, because the 20-cap is per trader rather than per household. However, Apex's risk team treats accounts traded by the same person (regardless of whose name is on them) as that one person's accounts. If you actually trade your spouse's accounts, those count against your 20-cap and the spouse's accounts may be banned for sharing. Each trader must trade only their own accounts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q125: Can I copy trade across my own Apex PA accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a125: Yes, within limits. Apex says "Copy trading across PA accounts under your personal name and business name is allowed," but the hedging rule still applies and all PAs must trade in the same direction. The cap is 20 active PAs across everyone in your household, your companies and connections, on Rithmic, Tradovate or WealthCharts. Going over 20 makes you ineligible for payout and can bring forfeiture, closure of all PAs and a permanent ban. Copying with other people is different: Apex's Prohibited Activities page lists sharing "trade copying with other traders" as strictly forbidden.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q126: Is copy trading from another trader's account allowed?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a126: No. Copy trading from another trader (signal services, follow-trader services, paid Discord rooms) is banned. Only your own strategies on your own accounts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q127: Will Apex monitor for hedging across spouses' accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a127: Yes. Apex's risk team uses IP, device fingerprint, billing address, and behavioral patterns to identify accounts being traded by the same person. Cross-account hedging detected between a trader's own accounts — or between spouses' "separate" accounts that are actually traded by one person — triggers the same ban as a single-trader violation.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q128: Can I use a VPN or VPS with Apex Trader Funding?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a128: Apex's rule targets the purpose, not the tool. Its Prohibited Activities page bans VPNs, proxy servers, cloud servers and anonymizing tools when used "for the purpose of misrepresenting, concealing, or disguising your identity, device, or location" to evade rules, hide violations or commit fraud. The same page forbids sharing "MAC addresses, computers, IPs" with other traders. A VPS does not change the separate automation ban: running an automated strategy on a cloud server is still prohibited at Apex.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_automation_title: Does Apex Allow Automated Trading, EAs, and Bots?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q129: Can I use a bot or automated strategy on an Apex evaluation or PA?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a129: No. Apex Trader Funding's Prohibited Activities page says "No Automation or Algorithm Usage allowed" and explains that rewards are meant for human traders, "not to reward automated systems executing preprogrammed logic." The page makes no exception for evaluations or Performance Accounts (PAs), so read it as covering both. Apex refers traders to its user agreement for the full wording and invites questions through its help desk. If any tool would place orders for you from preset signals, get Apex's answer in writing before connecting it to an Apex account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a130: We can't answer that on Apex's behalf. Apex's Manual Order Submission Requirement governs automated order placement generally, and whether a given EA — trader-owned or otherwise — falls inside or outside it is Apex's call. Check your current User Agreement or ask Apex support before running one on a funded account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a131: That's Apex's determination, not ours. Its Manual Order Submission Requirement restricts bots and scripts that place, modify, or cancel orders from preset conditions, and where the line falls for a specific bot — trader-owned or otherwise — is a question for Apex support or your current User Agreement, not something we can confirm from the outside.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a132: No. HFT is banned at Apex — typically defined as sub-2-second hold times, sub-second order rates, or any pattern that exploits simulation tick mechanics. Standard scalping (10+ second holds, 20-50 trades/day) is fine.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a133: No — explicitly banned. Latency arb exploits the gap between Apex's simulated quotes and real exchange prices, which is unfair to the simulation. Detection is reliable and bans are immediate.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q134: Are TradingView alerts and webhook automation allowed?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a134: We can't confirm that, and you shouldn't take our word for it either way. Apex's User Agreement includes a Manual Order Submission Requirement that restricts automated order placement, and a TradingView alert routed through a webhook bridge like PickMyTrade places the order on your Apex broker without a manual click at the point of execution. Read Apex's current agreement, or ask Apex support directly, before connecting a funded account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a135: No. Apex requires human supervision. A bot that runs unsupervised for days while you're on vacation violates the "actively monitored" requirement and risks account closure if detected.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q136: Can I use NinjaTrader strategies (NT8 .cs files)?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a136: Same answer as any other automated order-placement question: that's Apex's call, not ours. NinjaScript strategies fall under the same Manual Order Submission Requirement that governs bots and webhook bridges. Confirm directly with Apex or your current User Agreement before running one live.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q137: Can I use a copy-trading service across my own Apex accounts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a137: Apex has described an exception for copying trades you place yourself across accounts you own, as distinct from an independent bot or signal placing the order. PickMyTrade's Manual Trade Copier is built for exactly that shape: you place one trade, and it mirrors to your other connected accounts. That said, the scope of this exception is Apex's to define and can change, so confirm the current rule directly with Apex before relying on it. Coordinating with other traders on the same signal is banned regardless.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q138: What automation will get my account immediately closed?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a138: Apex has named HFT, latency arbitrage, news straddle bots, fully unsupervised 24/7 bots, copy-trading from another trader's account, and SL/TP-requirement violations as grounds for closure. Beyond that list, whether a specific automated setup — including a webhook bridge like PickMyTrade — falls inside or outside Apex's rules is Apex's determination, not ours. When in doubt, ask Apex support before you connect a funded account.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_platforms_title: Which Trading Platforms Does Apex Support?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a139: Tradovate (cloud-first, web + desktop + mobile), Rithmic (low-latency execution layer with R|Trader Pro front-end), NinjaTrader (charting + execution, especially popular for Apex), and WealthCharts (charting + order routing). Apex does NOT run on ProjectX — ProjectX went Topstep-exclusive in February 2026 and never adopted Apex.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q140: How do I set up my Apex account on Tradovate?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a140: Apex provisions Tradovate credentials when you activate your PA. Log in to the Tradovate web app or download the desktop client, paste in your Apex-issued credentials, and the account appears. The dashboard shows your trailing drawdown level in real time.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q141: How do I set up my Apex account on Rithmic?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a141: Apex provides Rithmic credentials and connection details when you activate. You connect through R|Trader Pro or any Rithmic-compatible front-end (NinjaTrader, Quantower, Sierra Chart). Pick the Chicago Area gateway for best latency.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q142: How do I set up Apex with NinjaTrader?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a142: NinjaTrader connects to Apex via either Tradovate or Rithmic underneath. Install NinjaTrader 8, open the Connections menu, add a new connection using your Apex Tradovate or Rithmic credentials, and the account appears. NinjaScript strategies and ATM Strategies work normally.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q143: Does Apex work with TradingView natively?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a143: Apex doesn't have a native TradingView broker panel — there's no "Trade Apex from chart" button in TradingView. The integration is through Tradovate (which IS in TradingView's broker panel for manual orders only). For Pine Script-driven automation, you need a webhook bridge.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q144: How do I connect TradingView to Apex via Tradovate?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a144: There are two ways. For manual trading: connect TradingView to Tradovate using the Tradovate broker plugin inside TradingView (a paid Tradovate subscription is required) and place orders directly from the chart. For strategy automation: use PickMyTrade, connect your Tradovate (Apex) account to PMT, generate a webhook alert in TradingView, and configure it so your strategy's buy/sell signals are routed directly to your Tradovate (Apex) account. You can also use PickMyTrade's Manual Trade Copier (available for Tradovate-to-Tradovate connections) to connect multiple Tradovate accounts simultaneously — trade on one leader account and PMT copies every trade, including OCO orders, to all connected follower accounts instantly. Note: the Manual Trade Copier is available for Tradovate connections only. If your Apex account runs on Rithmic, you can still automate multiple accounts simultaneously using a single TradingView alert — connect each Rithmic account separately in PickMyTrade.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q145: Can I trade Apex on ProjectX?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a145: No. Apex never adopted ProjectX as a supported platform, and as of February 2026, ProjectX became Topstep-exclusive. Apex traders execute through Tradovate, Rithmic, NinjaTrader, or WealthCharts only. If you see a tutorial claiming Apex-on-ProjectX, it is outdated or incorrect.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q146: Why am I getting Rithmic connection errors?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a146: Common causes: wrong gateway selected (use Chicago Area for Apex), VPN active (Rithmic blocks VPN), data feed agreement not signed, credentials still propagating after PA activation, or Rithmic-side outage. Try reconnecting after disabling VPN and re-checking the gateway. If persistent, contact Apex support.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q147: What's the difference between Tradovate and Rithmic for Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a147: Both are excellent platforms for trading Apex. Tradovate is a modern cloud-based platform with an easy-to-use interface available on web, desktop, and mobile, widely used among Apex traders for its simplicity. Rithmic is a professional-grade execution layer known for fast, reliable order routing, often preferred by traders who want more technical control. PickMyTrade fully supports Apex on both Tradovate and Rithmic.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q148: Can I trade the same Apex account on multiple platforms?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a148: No — each Apex account is linked to one platform at activation. You can have multiple Apex accounts each on different platforms, but a single account doesn't run on Tradovate and Rithmic simultaneously.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q149: Does Apex provide free CME data?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a149: Apex includes basic CME data on PA accounts. Real-time CME data on the trader's TradingView side requires a separate subscription ($7/mo retail bundle) — Apex's data and TradingView's data are independent.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q150: Can I use mobile apps with Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a150: Yes — Tradovate has full iOS and Android apps that work with Apex accounts. Order entry, position management, P&L viewing all work on mobile. NinjaTrader's mobile is more limited.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_pmt_title: How Do You Set Up PickMyTrade Webhooks for Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q151: Can I automate Apex with PickMyTrade?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a151: Yes, PickMyTrade supports Apex on both Tradovate and Rithmic. For Tradovate, use pickmytrade.trade. For Rithmic, use pickmytrade.io. To set up: connect your Apex broker account in PickMyTrade, then go to Generate Alert to get your JSON configuration and webhook URL. Paste the JSON into your TradingView alert message and add the webhook URL. Once configured, every time your TradingView strategy or indicator fires an alert, it is sent to PickMyTrade which routes it to your broker for execution.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q152: How do I connect TradingView alerts to Apex via PMT?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a152: For Tradovate: go to pickmytrade.trade. For Rithmic: go to pickmytrade.io. Add Apex as your broker connection and authenticate with your Apex credentials. Then use Generate Alert to get your JSON configuration and webhook URL. Paste the webhook URL into your TradingView alert and the JSON into the alert message. The alert fires, PMT receives it, routes to your Apex broker, and fills with a bracket order.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q153: Does PMT work with Apex on Tradovate?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a153: Yes, PickMyTrade fully supports Apex on Tradovate. Tradovate is widely used among Apex traders for its modern cloud interface, ease of setup, and availability on web, desktop, and mobile. Connect your Tradovate (Apex) account at pickmytrade.trade to get started.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q154: Does PMT work with Apex on Rithmic?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a154: Yes, PickMyTrade supports Apex on Rithmic. To connect, go to pickmytrade.io, add a new Rithmic broker connection, and enter your Rithmic username, password, and system name. Rithmic is popular among Apex traders who prefer professional-grade execution.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q155: Does PMT work with Apex on ProjectX or WealthCharts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a155: ProjectX: No — Apex does not support ProjectX (ProjectX went Topstep-exclusive in February 2026), so there is no Apex-on-ProjectX path to route through. WealthCharts: NinjaTrader and WealthCharts charting users typically still execute Apex orders via Tradovate or Rithmic, which is what PMT plugs into. The webhook URL pattern is unchanged.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q156: How fast is PMT alert to Apex execution?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a156: Sub-200ms median end-to-end (TradingView alert fires, PMT receives, broker API, fill confirmation back). Worst-case under load: 1-3 seconds. Compare to manual click-through of 10-60 seconds. The speed matters for Apex specifically because intraday trailing drawdown punishes slow fills.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q157: Can I automate multiple Apex accounts simultaneously with PMT?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a157: Yes — flagship PMT use case. PickMyTrade supports two ways to run multiple Apex (Tradovate) accounts simultaneously. First, automated multi-account: one TradingView alert automatically executes on all your connected Tradovate accounts at once — connect each account separately in PickMyTrade and a single alert fires to all of them with per-account quantity multipliers. Second, the Manual Trade Copier: connect one leader/admin Tradovate account with multiple follower/client Tradovate accounts. When you trade manually from the leader account, every trade — including OCO orders — is automatically copied to all follower accounts in real time. Any updates to TP or SL on the leader account are instantly reflected across all connected follower/client accounts. Note: the Manual Trade Copier is available for Tradovate connections only. If your Apex account runs on Rithmic, you can still automate multiple accounts simultaneously using a single TradingView alert — connect each Rithmic account separately in PickMyTrade.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q158: Does PMT auto-attach the mandatory SL/TP on Apex orders?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a158: PickMyTrade handles SL/TP in two ways. If your TradingView strategy already includes stop-loss and take-profit logic, PMT reads those values from the alert and forwards them to Apex. If your strategy only sends entry signals, you can configure SL and TP directly inside PickMyTrade when setting up your alert, PMT then applies those exit values to every outgoing order automatically.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q159: Will PMT alert me before I breach the trailing drawdown?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a159: You can protect yourself from breaching the drawdown by configuring stop-loss, take-profit, and trailing stop-loss on your trades through PickMyTrade, this ensures each position has defined exits before it can hit your drawdown floor. Additionally, if you want an extra layer of protection at the broker level, you can configure risk settings directly in Tradovate such as trailing max drawdown controls, which will close positions automatically when triggered.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q160: Does using PMT count as "automation" under Apex rules?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a160: Yes — semi-automated. The TradingView alert (your signal) fires, PMT routes it (the bridge), Apex broker executes (the fill). Apex permits this provided you're supervising. PMT is structurally semi-automated by design — you can override or pause at any moment.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q161: Can PMT enforce Apex's 4:59 PM ET flatten rule?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a161: PickMyTrade includes a Trading Time feature available across all supported broker connections. You can configure specific active trading windows with start and end times (24-hour ET format). Any TradingView alerts received outside your configured hours are automatically rejected — no new trades are placed. Existing open positions remain active. Settings can be applied to specific accounts or all accounts at once. For Tradovate connections, PickMyTrade also integrates with ForexFactory to automatically pause trading before and after scheduled news events — it can close open positions and cancel pending limit/stop orders during news windows.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q162: How much does PMT cost on top of Apex fees?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a162: $50/month per broker connection — covers all your Apex accounts (up to the 20-per-trader cap) plus any other supported brokers (Topstep, MFFU, Tradeify, Tradovate, Rithmic, IBKR, etc.). No per-trade fees. Start at pickmytrade.trade (Tradovate) or pickmytrade.io (Rithmic) for a free trial.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q163: How does Apex pay out winners?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a163: Apex 4.0 uses automated payout rails — ACH (US), Wise, Plane, and crypto (USDT/USDC). Request from your dashboard and the processor typically settles within 24-48 hours. Legacy 3.0 used a manual review process (mostly Wise/ACH) that frequently went into "Under Review" status and could take 7-14 days. The 4.0 automation eliminated most of that delay. The minimum payout amount is $500.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a164: 100% of the first $25,000 lifetime profit on a PA, then 90/10 split (90% to trader, 10% to Apex) on every dollar above that. The 100% threshold is per-account, not per-trader.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q165: When am I eligible for my first payout?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a165: After 5 qualifying trading days on Apex 4.0 (each must hit the minimum profit threshold for that account size). Plus you must be at least the minimum profit cushion above the trailing drawdown freeze level. Plus you must pass the consistency rule.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q166: What are the payout caps for the first 5 payouts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a166: The first 5 payouts follow a 6-step ladder that scales with plan size. On a $100K PA the ladder starts at $2,000 (payout 1) and steps up to $4,000 by payout 6, with smaller plans capped lower and the $150K capped higher. Caps exist to prevent immediate cash-out after one big day; on payout #6 onward the cap is lifted and traders are eligible for 100% withdrawal (the 50% consistency rule still applies on every payout). Verify the exact ladder for your specific account size in the Apex dashboard.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a167: From the 6th payout onward on the same PA, the dollar cap is lifted and traders are eligible for 100% withdrawal of available profits. The 50% consistency rule still applies on every request, however — it does not disappear with track record.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q168: What is the safety net rule for first 3 payouts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a168: For the first 3 payouts, you must maintain a "safety net" cushion — typically $100 above the trailing drawdown freeze level — after the payout is processed. So if a payout would put your balance below the safety net, the payout amount is reduced.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q169: What payout methods does Apex support?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a169: Apex 4.0 supports four payout rails: ACH (US bank transfer), Wise (international), Plane (international contractor payouts — replaced the Deel option in the 4.0 rollout), and crypto (USDT/USDC). Minimum payout is $500. Verify which rails are available for your country in the dashboard.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q170: How long do ACH payouts take?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a170: 1-3 business days through the ACH rail for US bank transfers on 4.0. International transfers via Wise or Plane take longer depending on country; crypto payouts settle within hours.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q171: Why does my dashboard say "PAID" but funds haven't arrived?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a171: Apex marks "PAID" when the payout processor (ACH/Wise/Plane/crypto) hands off the transfer, but the receiving bank's posting timeline is independent. ACH typically takes 1-3 business days after Apex's "PAID" status. Crypto is faster — usually within hours.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q172: Are payouts still going "Under Review" in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a172: Largely no on Apex 4.0 thanks to automated payout rails (ACH, Wise, Plane, crypto). Legacy 3.0 still occasionally hits "Under Review" status especially on large payouts. The 4.0 model was specifically designed to eliminate the historical Legacy 3.0 review delays.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q173: Why was my Apex payout denied?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a173: Top causes: consistency rule violation (best day too large vs total), insufficient qualifying days, KYC mismatch (name, address, ID document issue), safety net cushion not met (first 3 payouts), payout cap exceeded (first 5 payouts), or rule violation flagged on the account. Apex emails the specific reason; check the dashboard for details.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q174: Can I request multiple payouts in a month?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a174: Yes — once you've passed the first-payout requirements, subsequent payouts can be requested on a regular cadence. Apex doesn't enforce a hard "one per month" limit; some traders take weekly payouts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q175: Can I take a payout while holding open positions?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a175: No. The payout calculation uses closed-balance, and Apex requires the account to be flat at the moment of payout request. Close positions, wait for confirmation, then request.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q176: Does Apex withhold taxes from payouts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a176: No. Apex pays the gross amount and issues a 1099-NEC for US traders. You're responsible for self-employment tax (15.3%) plus ordinary income tax. Set aside ~30-35% of payouts for tax obligations.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_reset_title: What Happens If You Fail an Apex Account, and Can You Reset It?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q177: Can I reset a failed Apex evaluation?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a177: Apex 4.0: no — there are no resets. A failed eval requires buying a new evaluation. Apex Legacy 3.0: yes, paid resets are available. The 4.0 model deliberately removed resets in exchange for one-time fees and tighter rules.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q178: How much does an Apex Legacy reset cost?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a178: $80-$160 typical for Legacy 3.0 resets depending on account size. Verify current pricing on the Apex dashboard. Sometimes there are discount codes that apply to resets, sometimes not.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q180: What happens after my eval expires unfinished?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a180: Apex 4.0 evaluations have a 30-calendar-day hard limit. If you don't pass within 30 days, the eval expires and you forfeit the evaluation fee. No resets, no extensions — start a new evaluation if you want to try again.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q181: What's the easiest way to recover from a failed Apex account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a181: For 4.0: buy a new evaluation when a discount code is active (Black Friday, anniversary, weekly promos). Don't immediately re-buy — wait 24 hours, journal what failed, then start fresh with a clear plan. Most "blew 50 accounts" stories on prop firm forums are about not waiting and re-deploying broken discipline.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q182: What gets my Apex account banned?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a182: Cross-account hedging, copy trading from another trader, HFT, latency arbitrage, VPN use, account sharing, identity fraud (using someone else's KYC documents), credit card chargebacks. These trigger immediate account closure with no refund and may include cross-firm blacklist.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q183: Can I dispute an Apex charge with my bank?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a183: Don't. Chargebacks against Apex result in immediate account closure plus a permanent ban from Apex. They also flag you with the cross-firm prop blacklist. If you have a refund issue, work with Apex support directly.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q184: "Did I breach the trailing drawdown" — how can I check?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a184: Open your Apex dashboard or Tradovate platform and look for "BREACHED" or similar status. Apex emails within minutes of a breach. If you're on Intraday and your equity touched the trail at any point, you've breached even if price reversed afterward — the touch is what counts.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_misc_title: What About Apex Taxes, Mobile Access, Restricted Countries, and Comparisons?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a185: Yes — 1099-NEC if you're a US trader who received $600+ in payouts during the tax year. Apex distributes 1099s in late January / early February of the following year via the registered mailing address.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a186: 1099-NEC (Non-Employee Compensation). The income is contractor income, not capital gains. Reported on Schedule C of your tax return.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a187: Generally yes as a Schedule C business expense, especially if you're a consistent profitable trader (clear business intent). Failed evals from someone who never passes may be classified as hobby losses. Consult a CPA.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a188: Same as eval fees — typically yes as ordinary business expense if you have a serious trading business. Document each one for your records.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q189: Do I file Apex income on Schedule C?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a189: Yes for US traders. Apex payouts go on Schedule C as gross receipts, and you deduct trading-related expenses (eval fees, platform fees, data fees, automation tools, VPS, education) on the same Schedule C. Self-employment tax is calculated on Schedule SE based on net Schedule C income.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q190: Do I owe self-employment tax on Apex payouts?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a190: Yes — 15.3% on the first ~$168,600 in 2026 (verify SSA wage base for the current year), then 2.9% on amounts above. This is on top of ordinary income tax, which can push the total tax rate to 35-50%+. Set aside 30-35% of every payout for tax obligations.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q191: What countries are restricted from Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a191: Roughly 84 restricted countries as of April 2026. The list includes OFAC-sanctioned countries (Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus) plus some FATF gray-list countries and regions where KYC infrastructure is unreliable. Verify your country at support.apextraderfunding.com before purchasing.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q192: Can I trade Apex if I'm originally from a restricted country but live in the US?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a192: Generally yes if you have legal US residency and US-issued KYC documents (driver's license, SSN, US address). Country of birth doesn't disqualify you — current residency and KYC documents do.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q193: Does Apex have a mobile app?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a193: Apex itself doesn't have a branded mobile app, but Tradovate (Apex's primary platform) has full iOS and Android apps. You can monitor your Apex account, place orders, and manage positions from the Tradovate mobile app.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q194: Can I trade Apex on iPhone / Android?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a194: Yes via Tradovate's mobile app. Order entry, charts, P&L, drawdown level all visible on mobile. Mobile is fine for monitoring and emergency exits but most traders run their primary desktop setup for active trading.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q195: Apex vs Topstep — which is better in 2026?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a195: Apex 4.0 has more flexible rules (50% consistency vs Topstep's stricter rules, 5-day between-payout minimum vs Topstep's similar requirement, allows news trading), more platform options (Tradovate / Rithmic / NinjaTrader / WealthCharts vs Topstep's TopstepX + ProjectX exclusive stack — ProjectX went Topstep-only in February 2026), and one-time fees vs Topstep's monthly. Topstep has the OG reputation and slightly tighter integration. For automation specifically, Apex wins because TopstepX restricts third-party platforms.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q196: Apex vs MyFundedFutures (MFFU) — which is cheaper?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a196: MFFU's Core plan is generally cheaper than Apex's eval at the same account size, especially because MFFU eliminated activation fees entirely in July 2025. Apex 4.0 eval + activation fee combined sometimes exceeds MFFU's all-in cost. Both allow automation; MFFU is more permissive on copy trading.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a197: Tradeify 3.0 (March 2026) eliminated subscriptions like Apex 4.0 did. Tradeify's Lightning plan offers instant funding which Apex doesn't. Tradeify allows news trading freely; Apex 4.0 also allows it. Apex has bigger search volume and longer track record; Tradeify has won "Most User Friendly" prop firm awards. Both are reasonable choices.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q198: Did Topstep also halt metals like Apex did?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a198: Topstep restricted some metals contracts in early 2026, similar industry response to volatility. Specifics vary; check Topstep's permitted products list for current state.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q199: Can I run Apex on Mac?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a199: Yes. Tradovate has a native Mac client. NinjaTrader requires Parallels or a VM on Mac. Most Mac users go with Tradovate web or the Tradovate desktop app for Apex.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q200: What's the Apex Discord — is it official?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a200: Apex maintains an official Discord community accessible from the support site. Active community discussions, payout announcements, rule clarifications. Always verify "official Apex" Discord links from apextraderfunding.com — fake Apex Discords exist for phishing.
prop_firm_faq.apex_cat_gap_apex_title: What's New for Apex Payouts, Platforms, and Multi-Account Trading?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q201: How do I set up my bank for an Apex payout if I live outside the US?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a201: International payouts run through Plane, Apex's global payment partner, not direct ACH. After your first payout request is approved you'll get an email invitation from Plane (usually within about 1-4 business days) with a link to create your Plane profile and connect your local bank. Your bank account has to be in the same country you declared as your residency in Apex — if you live in, say, Spain, the bank has to be Spanish, or the transfer gets rejected. US-based traders skip Plane and use ACH, but the same matching rule applies: US residency, US bank. Always confirm current payout partners on Apex's official site since they occasionally change.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q202: My payout was rejected because my bank country didn't match my Apex profile — what now?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a202: This is one of the most common avoidable rejections. Apex requires the country on your declared residency to exactly match the country where your payout bank is held, on both US ACH and international Plane rails. If they don't match, the transfer is bounced even if everything else is compliant. Fix the mismatch first — either update your residency country in your Apex profile (if you genuinely moved) or use a bank in your declared country — then resubmit. You usually don't have to wait out a penalty period for this specific issue; it's a details problem, not a rule breach.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q203: At what exact point does my trailing drawdown stop trailing on a PA — with real numbers?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a203: On a Performance Account the trailing threshold follows your peak unrealized balance 1:1 until your peak hits the Safety Net, which is starting balance + drawdown + $100. Once you reach it, the floor locks permanently at starting balance + $100. Concrete example: a $50K PA has a $2,500 drawdown, so the Safety Net is $52,600 ($50,000 + $2,500 + $100); once your peak balance touches $52,600, your stop-out floor freezes at $50,100 and never moves again. A $150K PA (with a $5,000 drawdown) locks once peak hits $155,100. Until you reach that number you're still trailing, so the early phase of a PA is the riskiest.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q204: If I accidentally trade too many contracts on a funded account, do I lose the account?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a204: On an evaluation, an order above your max contract limit is simply auto-rejected and doesn't count against you. On a funded/PA account it's stricter: if you exceed the limit (commonly defined as going past your allowed size), you're expected to close the excess immediately. Leaving it on can get a pending payout denied and the account reset to the prior day's end-of-day balance, with several additional qualifying days required before you can request a payout again — and any profit earned from the oversized position can be removed. Deliberate "all-in" max-size gambling to beat the trail is treated as a serious violation and can forfeit the account. Verify the current scaling specifics on Apex's official site, as the numbers differ by plan.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q205: What's the difference between non-professional and professional market data on Apex, and will it cost me extra?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a205: Most retail Apex traders qualify as non-professional, and that real-time CME data is included in the plan with no separate exchange fee. If you don't sign or can't qualify for the non-pro agreement (for example, you're registered with a regulator or trade for a firm), you're classified professional and CME charges roughly $115+ per exchange per month on top of your plan. Level 1 data is included for non-pros; Level 2 / depth-of-market is an optional add-on (around $40/month on Tradovate). Confirm the current data fee schedule on Apex's official site since CME adjusts these.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q206: Can I trade during news releases like CPI or FOMC on Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a206: Yes — you can trade through economic releases using your normal strategy, and there's no news lockout window like some firms impose. What's not allowed is straddling both sides of a release purely to gamble on the spike (placing simultaneous buy and sell orders to catch whichever way it breaks), since that's treated as a prohibited windfall play. All news trades still have to respect the consistency rule and your drawdown, so a single huge news win can also skew your consistency math. Trade it like any other setup, not like a coin flip.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q207: Is there a minimum hold time on Apex, or can I scalp in and out in seconds?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a207: There's no minimum hold-time requirement — rapid scalping, opening and closing within seconds, is fine as long as you follow every other rule (consistency, drawdown, contract limits, and the daily flat-by-4:59-PM-ET requirement). What gets flagged isn't speed itself but patterns Apex considers exploitative, like coordinated both-sides hedging or pure latency arbitrage. So genuine fast scalping is allowed; just keep one winning day from ballooning past the consistency threshold. Always check Apex's official prohibited-activities list before pushing an unusual style.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q208: Why is my PA contract limit lower than what I had during the evaluation?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a208: This trips up a lot of newly funded traders: the funded/PA contract cap is intentionally smaller than the evaluation cap. For example, a $100K plan that let you trade 8 contracts in the eval typically allows fewer in the funded PA, and the $25K PA is the tightest, which is why many traders size that one in micros. Nothing's broken — Apex tightens size once real payouts are on the line. Plan your position sizing around the PA number, not the eval number, and check the current per-plan contract table on Apex's official site since these have changed across versions.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q209: Is 2FA mandatory on Apex now, and what happens if I lose my authenticator?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a209: Yes — since June 30, 2025, two-factor authentication is required for anyone who has passed an evaluation, so you'll enter a one-time code from an authenticator app (like Google Authenticator or Authy) every time you log in. Set it up the moment you pass, and save the backup/recovery codes somewhere safe, because if you lose the phone with your authenticator you'll need to go through Apex support to regain access, which can delay your trading. This protects your funded account and any pending payout. Use an app you back up rather than a single device you might lose.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q210: Can I have both a personal and a business account with Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a210: Yes — Apex allows one personal user account and one business user account per person, which is separate from the question of how many PAs you can run. This is useful if you want to keep trading income under a business entity for tax or bookkeeping reasons. The overall simultaneous-account cap still applies across everything you own, and the consistency rule is evaluated per account, not pooled. Confirm the current account-structure policy on Apex's official site before opening a second profile.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q211: When I copy trades across my own Apex accounts, does each one still have to pass the consistency rule on its own?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a211: Yes, and this surprises people. Copying your own trades across multiple PAs doesn't pool the math — Apex evaluates the consistency rule (your largest winning day staying within the allowed share of total profit) independently on each account. So if a copier multiplier makes one account's single day blow past the threshold, that account can be held back at payout even though your other copies look fine. The same goes for drawdown and contract limits: each account stands alone. When you scale a copier across accounts, check consistency per account, not just on the master.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q212: Can I automate copying one TradingView strategy to several Apex accounts at once with PickMyTrade?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a212: Yes. PickMyTrade can take a single TradingView alert and fan it out to multiple Apex accounts simultaneously over Tradovate or Rithmic, with per-account quantity multipliers so a $25K and a $150K account can each take size-appropriate positions from the same signal. That lets you run a one-to-many setup without manually firing each account. Just remember Apex applies consistency, drawdown, and contract limits to every account independently, so set sensible multipliers per account rather than blindly cloning size. For current connection steps, see PickMyTrade's Apex setup guide.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q213: Do I have to close my trades before the market closes at Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a213: Yes. Apex's trading times page says "All trades must be closed before 4:59 PM ET," and it is your responsibility to be flat by then. Agricultural futures close earlier (2:05 PM ET for livestock, 2:20 PM ET for grains), and holiday sessions can close early. Holding positions through the close is on Apex's prohibited list, and traders who do it "will forfeit their accounts and all associated balances." A new trading day starts at 6:00 PM ET.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q214: What do I need to request a payout on an Apex PA, and does a consistency rule apply?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a214: On EOD and Intraday PAs, Apex requires at least 5 trading days that each meet a minimum daily profit (for example $250 on a 50K EOD PA, $200 on a 50K Intraday PA), a $500 minimum payout, and a balance above the Safety Net, which is the drawdown limit plus $100. A 50% consistency rule applies: no single profitable day may be 50% or more of profit since your last approved payout. Each PA can receive at most six payouts, each with a cap, paid at a 100% split. Legacy accounts have their own rules.
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q215: How many contracts can I trade on Apex, and how many PAs can I hold?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a215: It depends on account size and stage. Apex EOD Evaluations allow 4, 6, 8 and 12 max contracts on the 25K, 50K, 100K and 150K sizes. EOD PAs allow 2, 4, 6 and 10, with tier-based scaling, so position size grows as your end-of-day balance moves up scaling levels. Apex lists "breaching the maximum allowed contracts per an account plan" as prohibited manipulation. You may hold up to 20 active PAs combined, and "There are no limits to Evaluation accounts."
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_q216: Can I trade during news like CPI or FOMC at Apex?
prop_firm_faq.apex_faq_a216: Yes, with your normal strategy. Apex's Prohibited Activities page says "Trading during news is allowed for your normal trading strategy." What it bans are news strategies that "chase the market" or place orders on both sides to gamble on the outcome. Its manipulation rule also names "non-directional bracket trading, where orders are left open on both sides of the market." Holding a long and a short at the same time during a news spike also breaks the hedging ban.
