tradingview_automation.faq_1_q: Does TradingView have built-in automated trading?
tradingview_automation.faq_1_a: TradingView charts your strategy and can send alerts, but it does not place live orders with your broker on its own. To turn a TradingView signal into a real trade you need an execution bridge. PickMyTrade is that bridge: it receives your TradingView alert through a webhook and places the matching order on your connected broker automatically.
tradingview_automation.faq_2_q: Can you execute trades directly on TradingView?
tradingview_automation.faq_2_a: Not for most futures brokers. TradingView can generate the buy or sell signal, but the actual order has to be routed to a broker that can fill it. PickMyTrade connects to Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation and more, so your TradingView alert becomes a live order without you clicking anything.
tradingview_automation.faq_3_q: How do I automate a TradingView strategy?
tradingview_automation.faq_3_a: Connect your broker account in PickMyTrade, generate the alert message and webhook URL, then create an alert on your strategy in TradingView. Delete the default alert text, paste the PickMyTrade message, and set the webhook URL in the alert's notifications tab. When your strategy fires, PickMyTrade places the order for you. Webhook alerts need a paid TradingView plan (Pro, Pro+ or Premium).
tradingview_automation.faq_4_q: How do I automate trades from TradingView alerts?
tradingview_automation.faq_4_a: Any TradingView alert can drive an order, whether it comes from a strategy, an indicator or a manual chart condition. You paste the PickMyTrade alert message into the alert and point its webhook at PickMyTrade. Each time the alert triggers, the order is placed on your connected account.
tradingview_automation.faq_5_q: What is the difference between automating a TradingView strategy vs an indicator?
tradingview_automation.faq_5_a: A strategy already knows its entries and exits, so its alerts can carry the full order and PickMyTrade places it directly. An indicator only signals a condition, so you set the entry, size and risk settings in PickMyTrade and the indicator alert simply triggers that pre-set order. Both work; the strategy path is more automatic and the indicator path gives you more manual control.
tradingview_automation.faq_6_q: Do I need a VPS to automate TradingView?
tradingview_automation.faq_6_a: No. PickMyTrade runs in the cloud 24/7, so there is no VPS to rent and nothing to keep running on your computer. Once your broker is connected and your alert is live, trades execute even when your machine is switched off.
tradingview_automation.faq_7_q: Which brokers can I auto-trade from TradingView with PickMyTrade?
tradingview_automation.faq_7_a: PickMyTrade supports Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, TradeLocker, ProjectX, Match-Trader, Tradier (Beta), cTrader (Beta) and Ironbeam (Beta). It does not support MT4, MT5, DXtrade or NinjaTrader.
tradingview_automation.faq_8_q: Is TradingView automation allowed on prop firm accounts?
tradingview_automation.faq_8_a: Prop-firm rules on automation vary by firm and change over time, and many futures firms treat automating your own strategy across your own funded accounts (internal automation) differently from subscribing to a third-party signal seller or letting someone else trade your account. PickMyTrade runs your own alerts on your own accounts, and works with Apex, Topstep, Bulenox, Alpha Futures, Take Profit Trader, FundedNext Futures, MyFundedFutures, TradeDay and Tradeify. Always confirm your firm's current rules before going live.
tradingview_automation.faq_9_q: How much does TradingView automation cost, and is there a free trial?
tradingview_automation.faq_9_a: PickMyTrade is $50 per month or $500 per year, and every account starts with a 7-day free trial that needs no credit card. The subscription includes unlimited tickers and 24/7 live support, and works with demo, live and prop firm accounts.
tradingview_automation.faq_10_q: Is automating TradingView with a webhook safe and reliable?
tradingview_automation.faq_10_a: Webhook automation is the standard way to connect TradingView to a broker, and PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side, though your total fill time also depends on your broker, network latency and how quickly TradingView sends the alert. Futures trading always carries risk, and automated systems can be affected by connectivity or configuration errors, so use stop-loss settings and test on a demo account first. More than 50,000 traders run PickMyTrade, with 28M+ trades placed through it.

vs_replikanto.h1_competitor: How It Works and the Alternative
vs_replikanto.subtitle: If you searched replikanto vs apex trade copier, you are comparing two NinjaTrader 8 copiers for scaling your Apex and other prop-firm accounts. This page explains how Replikanto copies to Apex, what its compliance and stealth modes really do, and where a cloud, no-NinjaTrader alternative like PickMyTrade fits.
vs_replikanto.intro_h2: What Is Replikanto, and How Does the Apex Use Case Work?
vs_replikanto.intro_p1: Replikanto, from FlowBots, is an order replicator add-on for NinjaTrader 8. You mark one account as the leader, mark the rest as followers, choose a copy method, and every order you place on the leader is mirrored to the followers. It supports up to 100 accounts and seven copy methods (Exact, Equal, Ratio, Net Liquidation, Available Money, Percentage Change and Pre Allocation), plus full ATM strategy replication.
vs_replikanto.intro_p2: The reason it shows up in searches for replikanto vs apex trade copier is prop-firm scaling. Traders who run several Apex Trader Funding accounts want one action to hit all of them at once. The Apex trade copier is the NinjaTrader 8 copier traders use specifically to copy across Apex accounts. Both are NinjaTrader-native, so the honest headline is this: replikanto vs apex trade copier is really a choice between two NinjaTrader 8 copiers, not between two different platforms. Two Replikanto features come up constantly in prop-firm circles: Stealth Mode obscures the order pattern so copying is harder to detect, while Compliance Mode (launched February 2026) does the opposite, disabling Remote Copy, Network Copy, Negative Ratio hedging and Stealth Mode so copying stays fully auditable. FlowBots states Compliance Mode gained approval from Apex Trader Funding and TopStep; treat any approval claim as a snapshot in time and confirm your own firm's current policy.
vs_replikanto.intro_p3: PickMyTrade takes a different approach. It is a cloud-based platform that connects directly to your broker (Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers and more) without requiring NinjaTrader, a VPS, or any software running on your computer. It also adds TradingView webhook automation on top of trade copying, which NinjaTrader-native copiers do not provide. PickMyTrade does not support NinjaTrader, so if your whole workflow lives in NinjaTrader 8, a NinjaTrader-native copier is the better native fit.

vs_replikanto.faq_1_q: How does Replikanto copy trades to Apex accounts?
vs_replikanto.faq_1_a: Replikanto is an order replicator add-on for NinjaTrader 8. You connect your Apex accounts in NinjaTrader 8, mark one as the leader and the rest as followers, then pick a copy method. When you place a trade on the leader account, Replikanto mirrors it to every follower account inside NinjaTrader. Because it lives in NinjaTrader 8, both the leader and the follower Apex accounts must be connected to NinjaTrader 8 for the copying to work.
vs_replikanto.faq_2_q: What do Replikanto compliance mode and stealth mode do?
vs_replikanto.faq_2_a: Stealth Mode obscures the order pattern so copy trading is harder for a broker or firm to detect, and it is most effective paired with the Market Only option. Compliance Mode, which FlowBots launched in February 2026, does the opposite: it disables Remote Copy, Network Copy, Negative Ratio hedging and Stealth Mode so that copying stays fully auditable. FlowBots states Compliance Mode gained approval from Apex Trader Funding and TopStep. Copy and automation rules vary by firm and change over time, so always confirm your firm's current policy before you rely on any mode.
vs_replikanto.faq_3_q: Do I need NinjaTrader 8 and a VPS to use Replikanto?
vs_replikanto.faq_3_a: Yes to NinjaTrader 8: Replikanto is a NinjaTrader 8 add-on, so it only runs inside NinjaTrader 8 on Windows and only reaches accounts that connect to NinjaTrader 8. A VPS is not strictly required, but most traders run Replikanto on a Windows VPS so copying keeps working around the clock without leaving a home computer on. That is a real running cost and setup step on top of the license.
vs_replikanto.faq_4_q: What is a good alternative to Replikanto that does not require NinjaTrader?
vs_replikanto.faq_4_a: PickMyTrade is a cloud alternative to Replikanto that needs no NinjaTrader 8 and no VPS. Instead of copying inside NinjaTrader, it takes a TradingView alert or a manual master trade and executes it across your connected accounts from the cloud, 24/7, even when your computer is off. It connects to Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, TradeLocker, ProjectX, Match-Trader, Tradier (Beta), cTrader (Beta) and Ironbeam (Beta). PickMyTrade does not support NinjaTrader, so if your whole workflow lives in NinjaTrader 8, a NinjaTrader-native copier is the better native fit.

PickMyTrade connects to Tradovate, Rithmic and ProjectX, the platforms many prop firms including Apex run on, so you can route your own TradingView alerts to those accounts from the cloud with no NinjaTrader involved. tv_tradovate.whatis_h2: What is TradingView to Tradovate automation?
tv_tradovate.whatis_p1: TradingView to Tradovate automation is the process of sending your TradingView alerts to your Tradovate account so trades execute automatically, with no manual clicking. TradingView is where you build and watch your strategy. Tradovate is where the futures order actually gets filled. On their own, the two only connect for manual click-trading, so a bridge is needed to carry each alert across and place the order for you.
tv_tradovate.whatis_p2: That bridge is a webhook. When your alert fires, TradingView sends a small message to a webhook URL. PickMyTrade receives that message, reads the symbol, side, size and any risk settings, and places the matching order on Tradovate. You do not write code, run a bot on your laptop, or rent a VPS. The whole flow runs in the cloud, so your alerts keep firing even when your computer is off.
tv_tradovate.whatis_p3: This is what lets a Pine Script strategy, a paid indicator, or a simple crossover alert trade a live, demo or prop-firm Tradovate account hands-free. tv_tradovate.faq_1_q: How do I connect TradingView to Tradovate?
tv_tradovate.faq_1_a: You can connect TradingView to Tradovate in two ways. TradingView's native broker link lets you place trades manually from the chart, but it does not run your strategy on its own. To auto-execute alerts, create a free PickMyTrade account, connect your Tradovate account, generate a webhook URL and alert message, then paste both into a TradingView alert. From then on every alert fires as a live order on Tradovate.
tv_tradovate.faq_2_q: Does connecting TradingView to Tradovate automatically trade my strategy?
tv_tradovate.faq_2_a: No. TradingView's native Tradovate connection is manual click-trading only. It shows your positions and lets you click to buy or sell, but it will not execute your indicator or strategy alerts on its own. For true hands-off, 24/7 automation you need a webhook bridge like PickMyTrade that receives each TradingView alert and places the order on Tradovate for you.
tv_tradovate.faq_3_a: Tradovate does not accept TradingView webhooks directly. A TradingView webhook is just an HTTP message, and Tradovate has no public endpoint to receive it. PickMyTrade acts as the bridge: TradingView sends the alert to PickMyTrade's webhook URL, and PickMyTrade translates it into a live Tradovate order.
tv_tradovate.faq_4_q: Do I need a paid TradingView plan to automate Tradovate?
tv_tradovate.faq_4_a: Yes. TradingView only allows webhook alerts on its paid plans (Pro, Pro+ or Premium). A free TradingView account cannot send webhooks, so it cannot trigger automated trades. Your Tradovate account can be a live, demo or prop-firm evaluation account.
tv_tradovate.faq_5_q: What does the TradingView alert message look like?
tv_tradovate.faq_5_a: PickMyTrade generates the alert message for you, so you do not have to write any code. You copy the JSON that PickMyTrade produces for your buy and sell signals, delete the default text in the TradingView alert box, and paste the PickMyTrade message in its place. That message carries the symbol, side, quantity and any stop-loss or take-profit settings you configured.

tradovate_copier.whatis_h2: What is a Tradovate trade copier?
tradovate_copier.whatis_p1: A Tradovate trade copier takes one source trade and mirrors it across several Tradovate accounts at the same time. Instead of placing the same order by hand on account after account, you set up the copier once and every entry, exit, stop-loss and take-profit copies automatically. That is the heart of copy trading on Tradovate: one decision, many accounts, no repeated clicking.
tradovate_copier.whatis_p2: Tradovate does have a native feature called Group Trade, but it only copies within a single login, it cannot run your TradingView strategy alerts, and it gives you no per-account risk control or cross-platform copying. That is why active traders reach for a dedicated trade copier for Tradovate. A tool like PickMyTrade adds TradingView webhook automation, per-account quantity multipliers, reverse and scale-in orders, and support for prop-firm and funded accounts on top of the raw broker connection.
tradovate_copier.whatis_p3: The Manual Trade Copier lets you place a trade by hand on your admin Tradovate account, and PickMyTrade instantly mirrors it, with matching stop-loss and take-profit, to every connected follower account. Below, you will find how it works, multipliers, prop-firm copying, setup steps and FAQs. Trading manually from TradingView instead, with Tradovate connected as your broker? tradovate_copier.propfirm_h2: Prop firm trade copier: copy across funded accounts
tradovate_copier.propfirm_p1: The biggest reason traders want a Tradovate trade copier is prop firms. If you run several evaluations or funded accounts, copying one signal across all of them is how you scale without watching every account by hand. PickMyTrade supports any prop firm that uses Tradovate as its trading platform, and lists 9+ Tradovate-powered firms, including Apex Trader Funding, Take Profit Trader, Lucid Trading, Tradeify and FundedNext Futures.
tradovate_copier.propfirm_p2: Here is the honest part most tool pages skip. Internal copy trading, routing your own TradingView alerts across funded accounts that you own, is allowed at most major futures prop firms. External copy trading, meaning subscribing to a third-party signal seller or letting someone else manage your funded account, is prohibited. PickMyTrade is built for the first case: it copies your own alerts across your own accounts, so you stay in control and stay compliant.
tradovate_copier.propfirm_p3: Firms also set their own limits on how many accounts you can copy across and how identical fills can be, and those rules change over time. Always confirm your specific firm's current rules on automated and copy trading before you go live.
tradovate_copier.multiaccount_h2: Multi-account trade copier: mirror one signal to unlimited accounts
tradovate_copier.multiaccount_p1: As a multi-account trade copier, PickMyTrade copies to unlimited Tradovate accounts under the same broker login on a single subscription, with no per-account or per-trade fee. If you trade through multiple broker logins, even with the same prop firm, each login needs its own subscription. That one nuance aside, you can run one strategy across a whole stable of accounts at once.
tradovate_copier.multiaccount_p2: The real power is per-account sizing. Every account gets its own quantity multiplier, and the math is simple: client position equals master position times the multiplier. So a 2-contract signal becomes 1 contract on a 0.5x account, 2 on a 1x account, 4 on a 2x account and 6 on a 3x account. Decimal multipliers like 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 are supported, and the final quantity rounds to a whole number.

Position size can be a fixed quantity or a risk percentage, so the copier fits both aggressive scaling and careful risk-first sizing.
tradovate_copier.futures_p2: Because it runs in the cloud, the futures fill lands fast and copies to every connected account within seconds. There is no desktop app to babysit and no VPS bill, which is a real difference from the older download-and-run copiers.

A tool like PickMyTrade adds TradingView webhook automation, per-account multipliers and prop-firm scaling on top.

tradovate_copier.faq_5_q: How do quantity multipliers work in the trade copier?
tradovate_copier.faq_5_a: Each account gets its own multiplier, so client position equals master position times the multiplier. A 2-contract signal becomes 1 contract at 0.5x, 2 at 1x, 4 at 2x and 6 at 3x. Decimal multipliers like 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 are supported, and the final quantity rounds to a whole number.

tv_copier.propfirm_h2: Scale one strategy across multiple prop-firm accounts
tv_copier.propfirm_p1: If you trade funded Tradovate accounts, this is where manual copying earns its keep. PickMyTrade already works with traders managing accounts across Apex, Lucid, Tradeify and other Tradovate-powered firms.
tv_copier.propfirm_p2: There is a compliance line worth stating plainly. Prop firms split copy trading into two buckets. Sending your own signals to funded accounts that sit in your own name is internal copy trading, and the major futures firms permit it. Handing your login to a signal seller, or trading someone else's funded account for them, is external copy trading, and that is off the table. PickMyTrade only does the first kind, so every prop-side destination should be an account you personally own. tv_copier.multiuser_h2: Copy to another trader's account, with their consent
tv_copier.multiuser_p1: A trade copier does not have to stop at your own accounts. Another trader can choose to receive your trades. The flow is deliberate and consent-based, and it is driven by them, not by you: they open their own PickMyTrade account, connect their own broker login themselves, and generate and share their own PickMyTrade token. You add that token as an external destination and set a size multiplier. They can revoke the token at any time and stop receiving trades. You never hold their credentials and never gain any authority over their account.
tv_copier.multiuser_p2: Each destination gets its own multiplier, so accounts of different sizes can each take the trade at a size that suits them: one at 0.25x, your own account at 1x, another at 2x, all from the same alert. There is no marketplace, no leaderboard, no published performance and no group code that strangers can join. The other person must generate and hand over their own token first, deliberately, from inside their own account.
tv_copier.multiuser_p3: One important line to hold: use multi-user copying for personal and live retail accounts. Prop firms only permit copying across funded accounts that you own yourself, so do not copy into someone else's funded account.

webhook_broker.secA_p1: A TradingView webhook is an outbound HTTP request that TradingView fires the moment a price alert or strategy alert condition is met. Instead of a popup or email, TradingView sends a JSON message to a URL you specify — in this case, a PickMyTrade endpoint that reads the payload and places the corresponding order at your connected broker.
webhook_broker.secA_p2: Webhook alerts are a paid TradingView feature (Pro, Pro+, or Premium plans) — the free plan cannot send them. Beyond that requirement, there is nothing to install: no VPS, no bridge software running on your machine, and no code to write.
webhook_broker.secB_h2: The Three-Hop Path From Signal to Order
webhook_broker.secB_step1_desc: A Pine Script strategy, a Pine Script indicator, or a manual price alert triggers. TradingView sends an HTTP POST containing your JSON alert message to the webhook URL saved in the alert's Notifications tab.
webhook_broker.secB_step2_desc: PickMyTrade's webhook endpoint authenticates the request via your account token, parses the JSON fields (symbol, action, quantity, risk parameters), and maps them to an order for your connected broker account — live, demo, or prop-firm evaluation.
webhook_broker.secB_step3_desc: The order reaches your broker through an OAuth-authenticated or API-key connection and executes under normal market conditions in well under a second end to end. Fills, rejections, and errors are logged back to your PickMyTrade dashboard.
webhook_broker.secC_p1: Every PickMyTrade webhook alert has two parts: a webhook URL (where TradingView sends the request) and a JSON alert message (what it sends). Both are generated for you in the PickMyTrade dashboard — you paste them into TradingView's alert dialog, you do not hand-write them.
webhook_broker.secC_url_label: Webhook URL — pasted into the TradingView alert's Notifications tab with the Webhook URL option enabled.
webhook_broker.secC_json_note: JSON alert message — pasted into the TradingView alert's Message field. A generated example:
webhook_broker.secC_field_symbol_desc: The instrument TradingView is alerting on, e.g. NQ1! for the E-mini Nasdaq continuous futures contract.
webhook_broker.secC_field_data_desc: The action: buy, sell, or an exit signal.
webhook_broker.secC_field_quantity_desc: Contracts or units to trade. Can also be sized dynamically via risk_percentage instead of a fixed number.
webhook_broker.secC_field_order_type_desc: MKT for market orders; limit and stop variants are also supported.
webhook_broker.secC_field_token_desc: Your account authentication token, generated per alert in the PickMyTrade dashboard — never shared across accounts.
webhook_broker.secC_field_multiple_accounts_desc: An optional array that fans the same alert out to additional connected accounts, each with its own token, account ID, and size multiplier — this is what powers multi-account trade copying from a single alert.
webhook_broker.secD_subtitle: The webhook path is broker-agnostic — the same TradingView alert format routes to whichever broker your account is connected to.
webhook_broker.secE_h2: Security and Reliability of the Webhook Path
webhook_broker.secE_p1: Because a webhook alert can place real orders, the connection between TradingView, PickMyTrade, and your broker is authenticated and encrypted at every hop.
webhook_broker.secE_card1_desc: Tradovate and other OAuth-supported brokers connect via OAuth 2.0 — PickMyTrade never sees or stores your broker password.
webhook_broker.secE_card2_desc: Account tokens and connection data are encrypted at rest and in transit (TLS/SSL).
webhook_broker.secE_card3_desc: Every webhook received and every order it produced is logged to your dashboard, with access controls modeled on SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria.
webhook_broker.secE_card4_desc: PickMyTrade targets sub-200ms execution from webhook receipt to order placement; real-world end-to-end latency (including TradingView's own outbound delay) typically lands in the 200–600ms range.
webhook_broker.secF_subtitle: Most webhook alerts that never execute trace back to one of these four causes.
webhook_broker.secF_item1_desc: Usually a TradingView plan issue — webhook alerts require Pro, Pro+, or Premium. Confirm the alert actually triggered in TradingView's own alert log before assuming PickMyTrade is at fault.
webhook_broker.secF_item2_desc: TradingView requires the Webhook URL checkbox to be checked in the alert's Notifications tab, with the URL pasted in — a checked box with an empty field, or vice versa, silently drops the alert.
webhook_broker.secF_item3_title: Invalid JSON in the Message Field
webhook_broker.secF_item3_desc: A missing comma or an extra brace makes the whole payload unparsable. Copy the generated message from the PickMyTrade dashboard rather than hand-editing it, and re-copy after any change to the alert.
webhook_broker.secF_item4_desc: Each token maps to one specific connected account. Reusing a token from a different account, or from a demo account against a live one, sends the order nowhere your broker recognizes.
webhook_broker.faq_1_q: What exactly is a TradingView webhook?
webhook_broker.faq_1_a: It's an outbound HTTP POST request that TradingView sends to a URL you specify the moment an alert condition is met. The request body is a JSON message you configure in the alert. PickMyTrade's webhook endpoint receives that request and converts it into a broker order.
webhook_broker.faq_2_q: Do I need to know how to code to use TradingView webhooks with PickMyTrade?
webhook_broker.faq_2_a: No. PickMyTrade generates both the webhook URL and the JSON alert message for you in the dashboard. You paste them into TradingView's alert dialog — there is no code to write and no Pine Script requirement.
webhook_broker.faq_3_q: Which brokers can a TradingView webhook route to through PickMyTrade?
webhook_broker.faq_3_a: Tradovate, Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, TradeLocker, ProjectX/TopstepX, Match-Trader, Tradier (Beta), cTrader (Beta) and Ironbeam (Beta). The webhook format is the same regardless of which broker your account connects to.
webhook_broker.faq_4_q: Do I need a VPS or to keep TradingView open for the webhook to fire?
webhook_broker.faq_4_a: TradingView needs to be able to evaluate your alert condition, which for most alert types does not require the browser tab to stay open once the alert is created. Once TradingView sends the webhook, PickMyTrade executes it cloud-side — you do not need a VPS or any bridge software running.
webhook_broker.faq_5_q: What TradingView plan do I need for webhook alerts?
webhook_broker.faq_5_a: A paid plan — Pro, Pro+, or Premium. TradingView's free plan cannot send webhook alerts at all, regardless of which automation tool you use.
webhook_broker.faq_6_q: How fast does an order execute after the webhook fires?
webhook_broker.faq_6_a: PickMyTrade targets sub-200ms execution from webhook receipt to broker order placement. End-to-end, including TradingView's own outbound webhook latency, most orders land in the 200-600ms range.
webhook_broker.faq_7_q: Can one webhook alert control multiple broker accounts at once?
webhook_broker.faq_7_a: Yes. The JSON alert message supports a multiple_accounts array, letting a single TradingView alert fan out to every connected account you specify, each with its own size multiplier.
webhook_broker.faq_8_a: Yes. OAuth 2.0 authentication (no stored broker passwords), AES-256 encryption at rest and in transit, audit logging, and account tokens scoped to a single connected account are all part of the webhook path.

webhook_broker.cta_subtitle: Generate a webhook URL and JSON alert in minutes, then paste them into a TradingView alert. 7-day free trial, no credit card required.

futures_trading_bot.secA_p3: This matters because futures move quickly. A trading bot for futures can react to a signal on the E-mini S&P 500 or Nasdaq the moment it prints, attach your stop-loss and take-profit, and manage the position while you are away from the desk.

futures_trading_bot.faq_1_q: What is a futures trading bot and how does it work?
futures_trading_bot.faq_1_a: A futures trading bot is software that executes a rules-based trading strategy on futures contracts automatically, so you do not have to place each order by hand. With PickMyTrade, the rules come from your own TradingView strategy or indicator. When your alert fires, TradingView sends a webhook to PickMyTrade, and PickMyTrade places the matching order, including entry, stop-loss, and take-profit, on your connected broker. It runs in the cloud, so trades execute even when your computer is off.
futures_trading_bot.faq_2_q: Does PickMyTrade provide the trading strategy, or do I bring my own?
futures_trading_bot.faq_2_a: You bring your own. PickMyTrade is an execution engine, not a black-box profit bot and not a signal-selling service. It runs the strategy you already have, whether that is a Pine Script strategy, a TradingView indicator, a manual chart alert, or a webhook from another tool. PickMyTrade never promises returns or a win rate, and it does not bundle a money-making algorithm. You stay in control of every rule.
futures_trading_bot.faq_3_q: Which futures brokers does the bot support?
futures_trading_bot.faq_3_a: Tradovate connects directly through PickMyTrade. Rithmic, Interactive Brokers, TradeStation, TradeLocker, ProjectX, Match-Trader, Tradier (Beta), cTrader (Beta) and Ironbeam (Beta) are supported through our partner platform, pickmytrade.io. Together they cover contracts like ES, MES, NQ, MNQ, and CL.
futures_trading_bot.faq_4_q: Can I run a futures trading bot on a prop firm account?
futures_trading_bot.faq_4_a: Yes. PickMyTrade works with demo, live, and prop-firm accounts on Tradovate, including Apex Trader Funding, Blue Guardian Futures, FundedNext Futures, My Funded Futures, Take Profit Trader, Top One Futures, Tradeify, and TradeDay. Each firm sets its own rules on automation and consistency, and those rules change over time, so confirm your current firm's policy before going live. PickMyTrade does not offer a way around any firm's rules.
futures_trading_bot.faq_5_q: Is a VPS required to run the bot 24/7?
futures_trading_bot.faq_5_a: No. PickMyTrade runs server-side in the cloud, so there is no VPS to rent and nothing to keep running on your computer. Once your broker is connected and your alert is live, the bot executes trades around the clock, even when your machine and the broker platform are closed.
futures_trading_bot.faq_6_a: Execution is server-side, not from your laptop. PickMyTrade processes your order in under 200ms on our side. Your total fill time also depends on your broker, prop firm, network conditions, and how quickly TradingView sends the alert, as with any automated system.
futures_trading_bot.faq_7_q: Can the bot manage stop-loss, take-profit, and daily loss limits?
futures_trading_bot.faq_7_a: Yes. You can attach stop-loss and take-profit using five methods, points or dollar value, percentage, price levels, ticks, or total profit and loss, add a trailing stop, and size positions by fixed quantity or risk percentage. You can also set daily risk limits and use a stop button to halt trading. These tools help manage risk, but they do not guarantee a profit or prevent every loss.
futures_trading_bot.faq_8_q: Are there extra costs beyond the PickMyTrade subscription?
futures_trading_bot.faq_8_a: PickMyTrade's own price is $50 per month or $500 per year, with a 7-day free trial that needs no credit card. Separately, your broker or prop firm may charge its own commissions, and trading live futures data from CME typically requires its own market-data subscription, priced by the exchange. Confirm current data and commission costs directly with your broker before going live.
futures_trading_bot.faq_9_q: Is a futures trading bot legal, and is it allowed by my broker and prop firm?
futures_trading_bot.faq_9_a: Automating your own strategy on your own account is legal and supported by regulated futures brokers such as Tradovate. Prop firms set their own rules, which vary by firm and change over time; many treat routing your own alerts across accounts you own differently from external copy trading or letting someone else manage your account. Confirm your specific broker and prop-firm rules before going live.
futures_trading_bot.faq_10_q: How do I set up my TradingView strategy as a bot?
futures_trading_bot.faq_10_a: Create a PickMyTrade account and connect your futures broker, set your risk settings such as stop-loss, take-profit, and position size, then generate the alert message and webhook URL in PickMyTrade. In TradingView, create an alert on your strategy or indicator, delete the default text, paste the PickMyTrade message, and add the webhook URL. Test it, confirm the fill in your alert log, then enable it. Webhook alerts require a paid TradingView plan.
